knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Dimensional Conic Primal–Dual Pair
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a closed convex cone, \(K^*:=\{y:\langle y,s\rangle\geq0\ \forall s\in K\}\), \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) linear, and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional conic linear optimization in inequality form; this definition constructs the dual but does not assert strong duality or attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The conic primal problem and its dual are the ordered pair \[(P)\quad p^*:=\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\{c^Tx:Ax-b\in K\},\] \[(D)\quad d^*:=\sup_{y\in\mathbb R^m}\{b^Ty:A^Ty=c,\ y\in K^*\}.\] Conic duality is the correspondence that replaces the primal cone order by the dual-cone multiplier condition and imposes \(A^Ty=c\), so every dual-feasible \(y\) supplies the lower bound \(b^Ty\) for the minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a linear objective and a constraint that the slack belongs to a closed convex cone, the conic dual maximizes the pairing with the right-hand side over multipliers in the dual cone whose adjoint image equals the primal objective vector. The pair is defined independently of whether either feasible set is nonempty, either value is finite, or either optimum is attained.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a closed convex cone.
\(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear, with data \(b\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((P),(D)\) form the conic primal–dual pair with feasible sets \(\{x:Ax-b\in K\}\) and \(\{y\in K^*:A^Ty=c\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Using \(u\succeq_K v\iff u-v\in K\), the primal constraint is \(Ax\succeq_K b\).
The dual objective is the best bound obtainable by scalarizing \(Ax\succeq_K b\) with an order-preserving linear functional.
special_cases_latex: For \(K=\mathbb R_+^m\), one obtains the standard inequality-form linear-programming dual.
For a self-dual cone \(K=K^*\), primal slacks and dual multipliers belong to the same cone.
immediate_consequences_latex: For every feasible pair \((x,y)\), \(c^Tx-b^Ty=\langle y,Ax-b\rangle\geq0\).
Dualizing the geometric conic form again recovers an equivalent primal problem when \(K=K^{**}\).
boundary_notes: Strong duality and attainment require additional hypotheses such as appropriate strict feasibility.
Sign conventions change if the primal cone inequality or optimization orientation is reversed.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Construction from a Cone-Induced Order
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a convex cone and define \(u\succeq_K v\) by \(u-v\in K\). Let \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional scalarization of a cone-ordered affine constraint under the nonnegative dual-cone convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A multiplier \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) is admissible for the order \(\succeq_K\) precisely when \[\langle y,s\rangle\geq0\quad\forall s\in K,\] that is, when \(y\in K^*\). Applied to \(Ax\succeq_K b\), such a multiplier gives \(\langle A^Ty,x\rangle\geq\langle b,y\rangle\). Imposing \(A^Ty=c\) converts this scalar consequence into \(c^Tx\geq b^Ty\). The cone-order dual construction is therefore \[\sup\{b^Ty:y\in K^*,\ A^Ty=c\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The cone order declares one vector above another when their difference lies in the cone. Its admissible scalarizing multipliers are exactly the vectors in the dual cone. Pairing the primal conic inequality with such a multiplier preserves the inequality. Requiring the adjoint image of the multiplier to equal the objective vector makes the resulting scalar inequality a lower bound on the primal objective, and maximizing these bounds defines the dual.
assumptions_latex: The primal affine constraint is \(Ax-b\in K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The order-preserving multipliers are exactly \(K^*\), and the induced dual is \(\sup\{b^Ty:A^Ty=c,\ y\in K^*\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(y\in K^*\iff u\succeq_K v\Rightarrow\langle y,u\rangle\geq\langle y,v\rangle\) for all \(u,v\in\mathbb R^m\).
\(K^*\) is the set of linear functionals nonnegative on every feasible slack direction.
special_cases_latex: When \(K=\mathbb R_+^m\), admissibility is componentwise nonnegativity \(y\geq0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every dual-feasible multiplier gives a valid global lower bound on the primal value.
If \(K\) is closed and convex, then \(K^{**}=K\).
boundary_notes: A componentwise nonnegative multiplier need not preserve an order generated by a cone other than \(\mathbb R_+^m\).
Reversing the cone inequality reverses the associated sign convention for multipliers.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the cone-constrained problem \(\inf\{f(x):b-Ax\in K\}\), every \(y^*\in K^*\) defines
\[
L(x,y^*)=f(x)-\langle y^*,b-Ax\rangle.
\]
If \(x\) is feasible, then \(L(x,y^*)\le f(x)\); hence \(\inf_xL(x,y^*)\) is a primal lower bound. For a primal-dual feasible pair with slack \(s=b-Ax\in K\), complementary slackness is
\[
\langle y^*,s\rangle=0,
\]
meaning that \(y^*\in K^*\) lies in the dual face orthogonal to \(s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual-cone elements are valid inequality multipliers. They generate lower bounds, while complementary slackness places the multiplier in the dual face orthogonal to the primal slack.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complementary Multipliers as Conjugate-Face Elements
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Facial and normal-cone geometry of multipliers complementary to a fixed slack.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a closed convex cone, \(s\in K\), and \(F=\operatorname{face}_K(s)\) the minimal face containing \(s\). Then the complementary multipliers are exactly \[K^*\cap s^\perp=K^*\cap F^\perp.\] This is the conjugate face of \(F\) in \(K^*\). With \(N_K(s)=\{u:\langle u,k-s\rangle\le0\ \forall k\in K\}\), \[\langle y^*,s\rangle=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad -y^*\in N_K(s)\qquad(y^*\in K^*).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multipliers complementary to a slack form the dual conjugate face orthogonal to its minimal face; their negatives are normal vectors to the primal cone.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional inner-product space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle y^*,s\rangle=0\iff y^*\in K^*\cap F^\perp\iff -y^*\in N_K(s)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual-cone multipliers are exactly the linear functionals monotone for the preorder induced by the primal cone.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complementary-Face Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Face-level refinement of the seed's slack–multiplier orthogonality statement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a face \(F\unlhd K\), let \(F^\triangle=K^*\cap F^\perp\). If \(s\in\operatorname{ri}F\) and \(y^*\in K^*\), then \(\langle y^*,s\rangle=0\) if and only if \(y^*\in F^\triangle\). The map \(F\mapsto F^\triangle\) reverses face inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiplier complementary to a relative-interior slack lies in the dual face orthogonal to the slack's minimal face.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual-Cone Multipliers and Their Orthogonal Faces
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a closed convex cone and let \(K^*:=\{y:\langle y,s\rangle\geq0\ \forall s\in K\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional multiplier geometry for the nonnegative-pairing dual cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dual-cone multiplier is a vector \(y\in K^*\). It defines the supporting halfspace \(H_y^+:=\{s:\langle y,s\rangle\geq0\}\), which contains \(K\), and the exposed conic face \[F_K(y):=K\cap y^\perp=\{s\in K:\langle y,s\rangle=0\}.\] For a conic primal slack \(s=Ax-b\in K\), the pair \((s,y)\) is complementary exactly when \(s\in F_K(y)\), equivalently \(y\in F_{K^*}(s)\). Thus multiplier geometry records both order preservation and the primal face annihilated by the multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiplier belongs to the dual cone precisely when it has nonnegative inner product with every primal cone direction. It therefore defines a supporting halfspace containing the primal cone. The primal cone elements orthogonal to the multiplier form an exposed face. A primal slack and dual multiplier are complementary exactly when each lies in the orthogonal face exposed by the other.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a closed convex cone.
\(s\in K\) and \(y\in K^*\) when complementarity is discussed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_K(y)=K\cap y^\perp\), and \(\langle y,s\rangle=0\iff s\in F_K(y)\iff y\in F_{K^*}(s)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(y\in K^*\iff K\subseteq H_y^+\).
For a feasible conic primal–dual pair, complementarity is the vanishing of the slack–multiplier pairing.
special_cases_latex: For \(K=\mathbb R_+^m\), complementarity is \(s_i y_i=0\) for every coordinate \(i\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(s\in\operatorname{int}K\) and \(y\in K^*\setminus\{0\}\), then \(\langle y,s\rangle>0\).
A nonzero complementary multiplier exposes a proper face of \(K\).
boundary_notes: The sign of the dual cone changes under the alternative polar-cone convention \(\langle y,s\rangle\leq0\).
Orthogonality alone is not complementarity unless the cone-membership conditions also hold.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Geometric Primal–Dual Cone–Affine Representation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a closed convex cone, \(\mathcal L\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) a linear subspace, \(b,d\in\mathbb R^m\), \(L:=\mathcal L-b\), and \(L_*:=\mathcal L^\perp+d\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional geometric representation of conic duality; objectives are defined up to constants induced by alternative shift representatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A primal–dual conic representation pair is \[(P)\quad \inf\{d^Ts:s\in K\cap(\mathcal L-b)\},\qquad (D)\quad \sup\{b^Ty:y\in K^*\cap(\mathcal L^\perp+d)\}.\] The affine feasible planes have orthogonal direction spaces, and the cones are dual: \(K^{**}=K\). If \(\mathcal L=\operatorname{Im}A\) and \(c=A^Td\), then \(s=Ax-b\) converts the primal to \(\inf\{c^Tx:Ax-b\in K\}\), up to an additive constant, while \(y\in L_*\) is equivalent to \(A^Ty=c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The geometric primal minimizes a linear functional over the intersection of a cone with a translated subspace. Its dual maximizes the paired shift functional over the intersection of the dual cone with an affine space whose direction is the orthogonal complement of the primal direction space. An ordinary matrix-form conic program is recovered by taking the primal subspace to be the image of the constraint map.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a closed convex cone.
\(\mathcal L\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a linear subspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed \((P),(D)\) constitute the geometric conic representation pair with dual cones and orthogonal affine directions.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(\mathcal L=\operatorname{Im}A\), \(y\in\mathcal L^\perp+d\iff A^Ty=A^Td\).
Changing \(d\) within \(L_*\) or \(b\) within \(-L\) changes the corresponding objective only by a constant on its feasible plane.
special_cases_latex: When \(K=\mathbb R_+^m\), the representation is the geometric form of linear-programming duality.
immediate_consequences_latex: The geometric construction is symmetric under exchanging \((K,L)\) with \((K^*,L_*)\).
The dual of the dual is an equivalent primal representation.
boundary_notes: The affine sets alone do not uniquely select the shift representatives \(b\) and \(d\).
This definition does not assert nonemptiness, boundedness, attainment, or equality of optimal values.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The equality-form primal conic program associated with \((A,b,c,K)\) is
\[
\operatorname{minimize}_{x\in E}\ \langle c,x\rangle
\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\qquad x\in K.
\]
Its feasible set is \(P=\{x\in K:Ax=b\}\), and its extended optimal value is \(p^*=\inf_{x\in P}\langle c,x\rangle\), using \(p^*=+\infty\) when \(P=\varnothing\) and \(p^*=-\infty\) when the objective is unbounded below on \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal conic program minimizes a linear functional over the intersection of a cone with an affine equality set.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(K^*=\{s\in E:\langle s,x\rangle\ge0\text{ for all }x\in K\}\), the dual conic program is
\[
\operatorname{maximize}_{y\in F}\ \langle b,y\rangle
\quad\text{subject to}\quad c-A^*y\in K^*.
\]
Equivalently, it maximizes \(\langle b,y\rangle\) over pairs \((y,s)\) satisfying \(A^*y+s=c\) and \(s\in K^*\). Its extended value is \(d^*=\sup\{\langle b,y\rangle:c-A^*y\in K^*\}\), with \(d^*=-\infty\) if the dual is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conic dual maximizes the equality multiplier's objective subject to the residual belonging to the dual cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Conic Form

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual conic linear form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual representation associated with the stated conic linear primal problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The conic dual is
\[
\max_{\mathbf y,\mathbf S}\ \mathbf y^T\mathbf b
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
\sum_{i=1}^m y_i\mathbf A_i+\mathbf S=\mathbf C^T,
\qquad \mathbf S\in K^*.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\sum_{i=1}^m y_i\mathbf A_i\preccurlyeq_{K^*}\mathbf C^T,
\]
where \(\mathbf Q\preccurlyeq_{K^*}\mathbf P\) means \(\mathbf P-\mathbf Q\in K^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual maximizes yᵀb subject to a slack equation whose slack lies in the dual cone. Equivalently, the weighted constraint matrices lie below Cᵀ in the order induced by the dual cone.
assumptions_latex: K^*\text{ is the dual cone associated with the primal cone }K.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{CLD}:\quad \max\left\{\mathbf y^T\mathbf b:\ \sum_{i=1}^m y_i\mathbf A_i+\mathbf S=\mathbf C^T,\ \mathbf S\in K^*\right\}.

children.top_down_role: Structural matching between primal and dual conic forms.

assumptions_latex: \(E\) and \(F\) are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces.
\(K\subseteq E\) is a nonempty closed convex cone, \(A:E\to F\) is linear, \(b\in F\), and \(c\in E\).
\(x\in K\) with \(Ax=b\) is primal feasible, and \(y\in F\) with \(s=c-A^*y\in K^*\) is dual feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle c,x\rangle-\langle b,y\rangle=\langle s,x\rangle\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Primal-dual objective gap at a feasible pair.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrangian correspondence and feasible-pair gap identity for equality-form conic programs.

source_refs.locator: 2 From Linear Programming to Conic Programming p. 43

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(L(x,y)=\langle c,x\rangle+\langle y,b-Ax\rangle\), the dual function is
\[
\inf_{x\in K}L(x,y)=
\begin{cases}
\langle b,y\rangle,&c-A^*y\in K^*,\\
-\infty,&c-A^*y\notin K^*.
\end{cases}
\]
Accordingly, its Lagrange dual is the associated dual conic form. For every primal-feasible \(x\) and dual-feasible \((y,s)\), where \(A^*y+s=c\), the gap identity is
\[
G(x,y)=\langle c,x\rangle-\langle b,y\rangle=\langle s,x\rangle\ge0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual function imposes the dual-cone constraint, and every feasible primal-dual pair has gap equal to the cone pairing of the primal variable and dual slack.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Conic Correspondence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasible Zero-Gap Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality certificate obtained from the conic feasible-pair gap identity without a constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in K\) satisfy \(Ax=b\), and let \((y,s)\) satisfy \(A^*y+s=c\) with \(s\in K^*\). Then
\[
\langle s,x\rangle=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\langle c,x\rangle=\langle b,y\rangle.
\]
Under these equivalent conditions, \(x\) is primal optimal, \((y,s)\) is dual optimal, and their common objective value is finite. Conversely, any feasible primal-dual pair attaining equal optimal values satisfies \(\langle s,x\rangle=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible conic primal-dual pair with zero cone pairing has zero objective gap and certifies optimality of both sides without a constraint qualification.
assumptions_latex: \(E,F,K,A,b,c\) define the finite-dimensional equality-form conic pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle s,x\rangle=0\) if and only if the feasible-pair gap is zero, in which case both feasible members are optimal.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible Zero-Gap Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero-Gap Feasible-Pair Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact optimality certificate supplied by a feasible primal-dual conic pair, without asserting existence of such a pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in K\) satisfy \(Ax=b\), and let \((y,s)\) satisfy \(A^*y+s=c\) with \(s\in K^*\). Then
\[
\langle x,s\rangle=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\langle c,x\rangle=\langle b,y\rangle.
\]
Either condition implies that \(x\) is primal optimal and \((y,s)\) is dual optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a feasible conic primal-dual pair, zero cone pairing is equivalent to equal objective values and certifies optimality on both sides.
assumptions_latex: \(E,F\) are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces and \(K\subseteq E\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle x,s\rangle=0\iff\langle c,x\rangle=\langle b,y\rangle\), and either condition certifies primal and dual optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Gap Feasible-Pair Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conic duality-gap slack identity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic identity connecting the objective gap and the primal slack for a feasible pair of the standard conic primal and dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \((x,\lambda)\) satisfying
\[
Ax-b\in K,\qquad \lambda\in K_*,\qquad A^T\lambda=c,
\]
let \(y:=Ax-b\). Then
\[
c^Tx-b^T\lambda=\lambda^Ty=\lambda^T(Ax-b).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every feasible pair of the standard conic primal and dual, the objective-value gap equals the inner product of the dual vector with the primal slack.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c^Tx-b^T\lambda=\lambda^Ty=\lambda^T(Ax-b)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Primal Equivalence of a Conic Lift
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates fiberwise primal equivalence from topological, qualification, and dual equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X,Z,E\) be finite-dimensional, \(K\subseteq E\) a closed convex cone, \(B:X\to E\) and \(C:Z\to E\) linear, and \(d\in E\). Set \[L=\{(x,z):Bx+Cz-d\in K\}.\] A lift is feasible-set exact for \(S\subseteq X\) when \(S=\operatorname{proj}_X L\). For an objective \(\widetilde f\) on the lift, fiberwise objective exactness means \[f(x)=\inf\{\widetilde f(x,z):(x,z)\in L\}\quad(x\in S).\] These two identities preserve the original feasible variables, pointwise value function, and primal infimum. They do not by themselves imply that \(S\) is closed, that either infimum is attained, that a particular constraint qualification is preserved, or that separately constructed conic duals have identical attainment properties.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact conic lift preserves projected feasible variables and fiberwise primal values, but this alone does not preserve closedness, attainment, constraint qualifications, or dual attainment.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq E\) is a closed convex cone.
\(B:X\to E\) and \(C:Z\to E\) are linear and \(d\in E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact projection and fiberwise objective equality establish primal equivalence only; stronger topological or dual conclusions require additional hypotheses.

notation.meaning: Projection of L onto the original variable space.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed Conic Lift with Nonclosed Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit finite-dimensional failure of closedness under conic projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[K=\mathbb S_+^2=\left\{\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\b&c\end{pmatrix}:a\ge0,\ c\ge0,\ ac\ge b^2\right\}\] and let \(P\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}a&b\\b&c\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)=(a,b)\). Then \[P(K)=\{(a,b):a>0\}\cup\{(0,0)\},\] which is not closed. In particular, \(X_k=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}1/k&1\\1&k\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)\succeq0\) and \(P(X_k)=(1/k,1)\to(0,1)\notin P(K)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projecting the closed cone of two-by-two positive-semidefinite matrices onto two entries produces a nonclosed feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb S_+^2\) has its usual finite-dimensional topology.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\) is closed but \(P(K)\) is not closed.

notation.meaning: Cone of real symmetric positive-semidefinite two-by-two matrices.

knowledge_statements.title: Closed Conic Lift with Nonclosed Projection

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent Conic Forms Can Have Different Slater Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary representation-dependent qualification boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The feasible set \(S=\{0\}\subset\mathbb R\) can be represented by the cone equality \(x\in\{0\}\), whose feasible point lies in \(\operatorname{ri}\{0\}\), or by \[(x,-x)\in\mathbb R_+^2.\] The latter representation has the same feasible set but no point with \((x,-x)\in\operatorname{int}\mathbb R_+^2\). Thus exact primal feasible-set equivalence does not preserve a representation-specific Slater condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two exact conic descriptions of the singleton zero can differ in strict-feasibility status.
assumptions_latex: Relative-interior feasibility is used for the zero cone.
Euclidean interior is used for the full-dimensional cone \(\mathbb R_+^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equivalent primal conic representations need not have the same Slater status.
knowledge_statements.title: Equivalent Conic Forms Can Have Different Slater Status

\(K\subseteq E\) is a closed convex cone and \(L=\{(x,z):Bx+Cz-d\in K\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=\operatorname{proj}_X L\) preserves primal feasible points and values, but does not alone preserve closedness, attainment, or dual regularity.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A lifted conic form is primal-value equivalent to the original problem precisely when
\[
S=\{x\in X:\exists z,\ Bx+Cz-d\in K\}
\]
and the lifted objective equals \(f(x)\) on every feasible lift. This equality preserves feasible original variables and the primal infimum. It does not by itself imply that the projected set is closed, that either formulation attains its infimum, or that their conic duals have identical attainment and gap behavior: linear projections of closed convex cones can be nonclosed, and constraint qualifications may hold for one representation but fail for another.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact conic lift preserves original feasible points and value, but projection and altered regularity can change closedness, attainment, and dual behavior.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Invertible Conic Reformulations Preserve Primal-Dual Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive equivalence boundary separating coordinate changes from noninvertible lifts and projections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:E\to E'\) be a linear isomorphism and \(K'=T(K)\). Replacing \(g(x)\in K\) by \(Tg(x)\in K'\) preserves feasibility, primal attainment, and relative strict feasibility. Multipliers correspond by \(y'^*=T^{-*}y^*\), with \(\langle y'^*,Tg(x)\rangle=\langle y^*,g(x)\rangle\); consequently the associated dual objectives, gaps, dual attainment, and complementarity are preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible change of conic coordinates preserves primal and dual behavior; noninvertible lifting or projection need not.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq E\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y^*\longleftrightarrow T^{-*}y^*\text{ gives a pairing- and value-preserving primal-dual equivalence}.

notation.meaning: Inverse adjoint transporting multipliers from E to E'

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal-Value Equivalence of an Exact Conic Lift
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Precisely separates primal equivalence from dual and topological equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X,Z,E\) be finite-dimensional spaces, \(K\subseteq E\) a closed convex cone, \(B:X\to E\) and \(C:Z\to E\) linear, and \(d\in E\). A lift \[L=\{(x,z)\in X\times Z:Bx+Cz-d\in K\}\] with objective \(\widetilde f(x,z)\) is primal-value equivalent to \(\inf_{x\in S}f(x)\) when \[S=\operatorname{proj}_X L\quad\text{and}\quad \inf\{\widetilde f(x,z):(x,z)\in L\}=\inf_{x\in S}f(x).\] The stronger fiberwise condition \(\widetilde f(x,z)=f(x)\) for every \((x,z)\in L\) guarantees the value identity. Neither condition alone guarantees closedness of \(S\), attainment, Slater regularity, or equivalence of the associated conic duals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact lift preserves projected feasible variables and the primal value, but those identities alone do not preserve closedness, attainment, constraint qualifications, or dual behavior.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq E\) is a closed convex cone.
\(B:X\to E\) and \(C:Z\to E\) are linear and \(d\in E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact projection plus objective-value preservation gives primal-value equivalence only; additional regularity is required for topological or dual equivalence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Specialization of the Generic Conic Dual Template
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider the generic pair \(\inf\{c^Tx:Ax-b\in K\}\) and \(\sup\{b^Ty:A^Ty=c,\ y\in K^*\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interface-level specialization to LP, second-order-cone, and semidefinite models; it does not develop the modeling theory of those classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A conic-duality specialization is obtained by selecting a concrete cone and its pairing: \[K=\mathbb R_+^m,\qquad K=\prod_{i=1}^q\mathcal Q_{r_i},\qquad\text{or}\qquad K=\mathbb S_+^r,\] where \(\mathcal Q_r:=\{(u,t):\|u\|_2\leq t\}\) and matrices use \(\langle X,Y\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(XY)\). These cones are self-dual, so the dual template retains the same cone type for its multipliers. The resulting pairs are, respectively, linear-programming, second-order-cone, and semidefinite primal–dual representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The generic conic dual is specialized by substituting a standard cone and its natural inner product. The nonnegative orthant produces linear programming, a product of Lorentz cones produces second-order-cone programming, and the positive-semidefinite cone with trace pairing produces semidefinite programming. Each listed cone is self-dual, so its dual multipliers have the same structural cone constraint as the primal slacks.
assumptions_latex: The generic conic primal–dual template is expressed using a closed convex cone and its dual.
For the matrix specialization, the ambient space is \(\mathbb S^r\) with trace pairing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Substitution of \(\mathbb R_+^m\), \(\prod_i\mathcal Q_{r_i}\), or \(\mathbb S_+^r\) yields the LP, SOCP, or SDP dual pair, respectively.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The specialization map replaces the abstract memberships \(s\in K\), \(y\in K^*\) by coordinate inequalities, Lorentz inequalities, or positive-semidefinite inequalities.

Because \((\mathbb R_+^n)^*=\mathbb R_+^n\), the conic pair specializes to
\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\},
\qquad
\max_{y\in\mathbb R^m}\{b^Ty:A^Ty\le c\}.

For every feasible \(x,y\), weak duality gives \(b^Ty\le c^Tx\). If both programs are feasible, their optimal values are finite, each program has an optimal solution, and the values coincide. A feasible pair \((x,y)\) is optimal exactly when its slack \(s=c-A^Ty\ge0\) satisfies \(x^Ts=0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear-Programming Feasibility and Unboundedness Alternatives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Status alternatives for the equality-form primal and inequality-form dual linear programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[
(P)\quad\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\},
\qquad
(D)\quad\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty\le c\}.
\]
If \((P)\) is feasible, then either \((D)\) is feasible and both programs attain a common finite optimum, or \((D)\) is infeasible and \((P)\) is unbounded below. Symmetrically, if \((D)\) is feasible, then either \((P)\) is feasible and both programs attain a common finite optimum, or \((P)\) is infeasible and \((D)\) is unbounded above. Both programs may be infeasible; for example, \(A=[0]\), \(b=1\), and \(c=-1\) give \(0x=1\) in \((P)\) and \(0y\le-1\) in \((D)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an LP dual pair, feasibility of one side and infeasibility of the other forces the feasible side to be unbounded; both sides can instead be infeasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: One-sided feasibility with opposite-side infeasibility forces unboundedness of the feasible side, while simultaneous infeasibility is possible.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear-Programming Dual Status Alternatives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Status refinement of equality-form LP duality beyond the case where both sides are feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[
(P)\quad\inf\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\},
\qquad
(D)\quad\sup\{b^Ty:A^Ty\le c\},
\]
if either problem is feasible with a finite optimal value, both problems attain optimal solutions and their values are equal. If \((P)\) is unbounded below, then \((D)\) is infeasible; if \((D)\) is unbounded above, then \((P)\) is infeasible. Hence, if one problem is feasible and the other infeasible, the feasible problem is unbounded in its optimization direction. Both problems can be infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LP duality has exact status alternatives: finite solvability transfers with equal attained values, unboundedness forces opposite-side infeasibility, and both sides can be infeasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite solvability on either side implies equal attained optima; unboundedness on either side implies infeasibility of the opposite side.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inequality-Form Linear Primal–Dual Pair
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), with vector inequalities interpreted componentwise.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional linear programming in minimization, greater-than inequality form with unrestricted primal variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The linear-programming primal–dual pair is \[(P_{\rm LP})\quad p^*:=\inf\{c^Tx:Ax\geq b,\ x\in\mathbb R^n\},\] \[(D_{\rm LP})\quad d^*:=\sup\{b^Ty:A^Ty=c,\ y\geq0\}.\] It is the conic pair associated with the self-dual cone \(\mathbb R_+^m\). A primal-feasible \(x\) and dual-feasible \(y\) have gap \[c^Tx-b^Ty=y^T(Ax-b)\geq0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an LP that minimizes a linear objective subject to componentwise lower inequalities, the dual maximizes the right-hand-side pairing over nonnegative multipliers whose transpose image equals the objective vector. This is conic duality over the nonnegative orthant. The gap between any feasible primal and dual objectives equals the nonnegative multiplier–slack product.
assumptions_latex: The primal variables are unrestricted and the inequalities are \(Ax\geq b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The canonical dual is \(\sup\{b^Ty:A^Ty=c,\ y\geq0\}\), with feasible-pair gap \(y^T(Ax-b)\geq0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: A free primal variable produces a dual equality \(A^Ty=c\).
The same pair is obtained by setting \(K=K^*=\mathbb R_+^m\) in the conic template.
special_cases_latex: Equality constraints may be encoded by paired opposite inequalities; the associated net multiplier is unrestricted.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every dual-feasible \(y\) certifies the lower bound \(d^*\leq b^Ty\leq p^*\) with the middle inequality interpreted pointwise against every primal-feasible \(x\).
Zero feasible-pair gap implies optimality of both feasible points.
boundary_notes: Other standard forms have different sign and variable restrictions but are equivalent after elementary transformations.
The definition of the pair is distinct from the LP strong-duality theorem.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear Programming Weak and Strong Duality with Complementarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Duality and optimality characterization for the standard equality-form primal LP and its dual, including empty and unbounded regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}$ and $D=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^m:A^\top y\leq c\}$. Then: (i) $c^\top x\geq b^\top y$ for every $x\in P$ and $y\in D$; (ii) if $P\neq\varnothing$ or $D\neq\varnothing$, then
\[\inf_{x\in P}c^\top x=\sup_{y\in D}b^\top y,\]
with $\inf\varnothing=+\infty$ and $\sup\varnothing=-\infty$. The common value is finite if and only if both $P$ and $D$ are nonempty, and then both optima are attained. Moreover, for $x\in P$ and $y\in D$, both are optimal if and only if $x_j(c-A^\top y)_j=0$ for every $j=1,\ldots,n$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every primal feasible value is at least every dual feasible value. If at least one feasible region is nonempty, the extended primal and dual values agree. This value is finite exactly when both sides are feasible, in which case both attain optima. A feasible primal–dual pair is jointly optimal exactly when each primal variable times its corresponding dual slack is zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall x\in P,\forall y\in D:\ c^\top x\geq b^\top y;\quad P\neq\varnothing\lor D\neq\varnothing\Rightarrow\inf_{x\in P}c^\top x=\sup_{y\in D}b^\top y;\quad x,y\text{ optimal}\iff\forall j,\ x_j(c-A^\top y)_j=0

Each Lorentz cone \(Q_n=\{(t,u)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{n-1}:t\ge\|u\|_2\}\) is self-dual, so a second-order cone program and its dual use the same product cone \(K=\prod_{i=1}^r Q_{n_i}\). For the pair
\[
\min\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=b,\ x\in K\},
\qquad
\max\{\langle b,y\rangle:c-A^*y\in K\},
\]
if there exist \(x_0\in\operatorname{int}K\) with \(Ax_0=b\) and \(y_0\in F\) with \(c-A^*y_0\in\operatorname{int}K\), then both optima are attained and \(p^*=d^*\). Every optimal feasible triple \((x,y,s)\), with \(s=c-A^*y\), satisfies \(\langle x,s\rangle=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Second-order cones are self-dual; two-sided strict feasibility yields equal attained primal and dual values, with complementary cone pairing.
knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Cone Duality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lorentz-Block Complementarity Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blockwise geometric form of complementary slackness for product second-order cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_i=(t_i,u_i)\in Q_{n_i}\) and \(s_i=(\tau_i,v_i)\in Q_{n_i}\). For \(x=(x_i)_i\) and \(s=(s_i)_i\),
\[
\langle x,s\rangle=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\langle x_i,s_i\rangle=0\quad\text{for every }i.
\]
For each block with \(x_i\ne0\) and \(s_i\ne0\), block complementarity is equivalent to
\[
t_i=\|u_i\|_2>0,
\qquad \tau_i=\|v_i\|_2>0,
\qquad v_i=-\frac{\tau_i}{t_i}u_i.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Product-cone complementarity is blockwise; two nonzero complementary Lorentz vectors are boundary vectors with oppositely directed spatial parts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle x,s\rangle=0\) holds exactly blockwise, with antiparallel boundary geometry on every nonzero complementary block.
knowledge_statements.title: Lorentz-Block Complementarity Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal Slater Does Not Ensure Primal Attainment in SOCP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit failure of same-side attainment under only primal strict feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(Q_3=\{(t,u,v):t\ge\sqrt{u^2+v^2}\}\), the second-order-cone program
\[
\inf\{t-u:(t,u,v)\in Q_3,\ v=1\}
\]
is strictly feasible and has finite value \(0\), but no feasible point attains that value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly feasible SOCP can have a finite unattained primal infimum, so primal Slater guarantees opposite-side attainment rather than primal attainment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^*=0\), the primal is strictly feasible, and no primal optimizer exists.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Slater Does Not Ensure Primal Attainment in SOCP

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Side-specific strong-duality and attainment consequences for the equality-form SOCP pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the second-order-cone pair in the seed, if there exists \(x_0\in\operatorname{int}K\) with \(Ax_0=b\) and \(p^*>-\infty\), then \(p^*=d^*\) and the dual optimum is attained. Dually, if there exists \(y_0\) with \(c-A^*y_0\in\operatorname{int}K\) and \(d^*<+\infty\), then \(p^*=d^*\) and the primal optimum is attained. Strict feasibility on one side alone does not ensure attainment on that same side.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal strict feasibility yields zero gap and dual attainment, while dual strict feasibility yields zero gap and primal attainment; same-side attainment requires more.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a finite product of Lorentz cones and the primal-dual pair has the equality form stated in the seed.
The relevant side is strictly feasible and has the indicated finite value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Primal Slater implies \(p^*=d^*\) with dual attainment; dual Slater implies \(p^*=d^*\) with primal attainment.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-Order-Cone Primal–Dual Pair
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(r\geq2\), let \(\mathcal Q_r:=\{(u,t)\in\mathbb R^{r-1}\times\mathbb R:\|u\|_2\leq t\}\). Let \(K:=\prod_{i=1}^q\mathcal Q_{r_i}\), which is self-dual under the Euclidean inner product.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional SOCP with a product of Lorentz cones and a linear objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For block maps \(A_i\) and vectors \(b_i\), the SOCP primal is \[(P_{\rm soc})\quad \inf_x\left\{c^Tx:A_ix-b_i\in\mathcal Q_{r_i},\ i=1,\ldots,q\right\}.\] Because \(K^*=K\), its dual is \[(D_{\rm soc})\quad \sup_{y_1,\ldots,y_q}\left\{\sum_{i=1}^q b_i^Ty_i:\sum_{i=1}^qA_i^Ty_i=c,\ y_i\in\mathcal Q_{r_i}\right\}.\] Each primal cone constraint may equivalently be written \(\|D_ix-d_i\|_2\leq p_i^Tx-q_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A second-order-cone program has a linear objective and affine slacks constrained to Lorentz cones. Since every Lorentz cone and their finite product are self-dual, the dual multipliers satisfy Lorentz-cone constraints of the same block sizes, together with one adjoint balance equation. The usual norm-inequality representation is equivalent to Lorentz-cone membership.
assumptions_latex: The primal slack is partitioned into blocks \(A_ix-b_i\in\mathbb R^{r_i}\).
The Euclidean inner product is used on every block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The canonical SOCP dual has balance equation \(\sum_iA_i^Ty_i=c\) and block constraints \(y_i\in\mathcal Q_{r_i}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \((u,t)\in\mathcal Q_r\iff\|u\|_2\leq t\).
\(K^*=K\) for \(K=\prod_i\mathcal Q_{r_i}\).
special_cases_latex: \(\mathcal Q_2\) is linearly isomorphic to \(\mathbb R_+^2\), while higher-dimensional Lorentz cones are nonpolyhedral.
immediate_consequences_latex: For feasible \(x\) and \((y_i)_i\), the gap is \(\sum_i\langle y_i,A_ix-b_i\rangle\geq0\).
Zero gap is equivalent to blockwise complementarity because every block pairing is nonnegative.
boundary_notes: Rotated second-order cones require a linear isomorphism or their own explicit cone notation.
Strong duality is not automatic merely from self-duality of the cone.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the trace inner product, \((\mathbb S_+^n)^*=\mathbb S_+^n\). Hence the semidefinite primal-dual pair is
\[
\min_{X\succeq0}\{\langle C,X\rangle:\langle A_i,X\rangle=b_i\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,m\},
\qquad
\max_{y\in\mathbb R^m}\left\{b^Ty:C-\sum_{i=1}^m y_iA_i\succeq0\right\}.
\]
If the stated primal and dual strictly feasible points exist, both programs attain their optima and \(p^*=d^*\). For every feasible \((X,y,S)\), where \(S=C-\sum_{i=1}^m y_iA_i\), the objective gap equals \(\langle X,S\rangle\ge0\); consequently, feasibility together with \(\langle X,S\rangle=0\) characterizes optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The positive-semidefinite cone is self-dual; two-sided strict feasibility gives attained strong duality and trace complementary slackness.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent Matrix Complementarity Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-geometric refinement of trace complementary slackness for positive-semidefinite primal and dual slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(X,S\in\mathbb S_+^n\), the following conditions are equivalent:
\[
\operatorname{tr}(XS)=0,
\qquad X^{1/2}SX^{1/2}=0,
\qquad XS=SX=0,
\qquad \operatorname{range}(X)\perp\operatorname{range}(S).
\]
Consequently, a feasible SDP primal-dual pair has zero objective gap exactly when its primal matrix and dual slack have orthogonal ranges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For PSD matrices, trace complementarity is equivalent to a zero matrix product and orthogonality of their ranges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle X,S\rangle=0\iff XS=0\iff\operatorname{range}(X)\perp\operatorname{range}(S)\).

notation.meaning: Trace inner product on symmetric matrices.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semidefinite Primal–Dual Pair under Trace Pairing
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathbb S^r\) be the real symmetric matrices with \(\langle X,Y\rangle:=\operatorname{tr}(XY)\), and let \(\mathbb S_+^r\) be the self-dual positive-semidefinite cone. Set \(\mathcal A x:=\sum_{j=1}^n x_jA_j\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional semidefinite programming in affine-matrix-inequality form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(A_1,\ldots,A_n,B\in\mathbb S^r\) and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), the semidefinite primal–dual pair is \[(P_{\rm sdp})\quad \inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\{c^Tx:\mathcal A x-B\succeq0\},\] \[(D_{\rm sdp})\quad \sup_{Y\in\mathbb S^r}\{\operatorname{tr}(BY):\operatorname{tr}(A_jY)=c_j\ (j=1,\ldots,n),\ Y\succeq0\}.\] The adjoint satisfies \(\mathcal A^*Y=(\operatorname{tr}(A_1Y),\ldots,\operatorname{tr}(A_nY))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SDP minimizes a linear function subject to an affine symmetric matrix being positive semidefinite. Under the trace inner product, the positive-semidefinite cone is self-dual. Hence the dual variable is a positive-semidefinite matrix, its trace pairings with the coefficient matrices reproduce the primal objective coefficients, and its trace pairing with the constant matrix is maximized.
assumptions_latex: The matrix space uses the trace inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The canonical dual is \(\sup\{\operatorname{tr}(BY):\mathcal A^*Y=c,\ Y\succeq0\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Dual feasibility is \(Y\succeq0\) together with \(\operatorname{tr}(A_jY)=c_j\) for every \(j\).
For feasible \((x,Y)\), the gap is \(\operatorname{tr}(Y(\mathcal A x-B))\).
special_cases_latex: Diagonal coefficient matrices reduce the semidefinite cone constraint to componentwise linear inequalities.
immediate_consequences_latex: The feasible-pair gap is nonnegative.
Complementarity is \(\operatorname{tr}(YS)=0\) for \(S=\mathcal A x-B\succeq0\); for positive-semidefinite \(S,Y\), this is equivalent to \(SY=YS=0\).
boundary_notes: Strict feasibility or another constraint qualification is needed for standard strong-duality conclusions.
Complex Hermitian SDP uses the Hermitian trace pairing and is outside this real-symmetric formulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal Value, Dual Value, Gap, and Attainment
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((P)\) be a minimization problem with feasible set \(X\) and objective \(f\), and let \((D)\) be an associated maximization dual with feasible set \(Y\) and objective \(g\). Values lie in the extended real line.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Min-primal/max-dual convention; value equality and attainment are treated as logically separate properties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[p^*:=\inf_{x\in X}f(x),\qquad d^*:=\sup_{y\in Y}g(y).\] When both values are finite, the value duality gap is \(\Delta^*:=p^*-d^*\). The primal value is attained when \(\operatorname{Argmin}_X f:=\{x\in X:f(x)=p^*\}\neq\varnothing\); the dual value is attained when \(\operatorname{Argmax}_Y g:=\{y\in Y:g(y)=d^*\}\neq\varnothing\). Weak duality is \(d^*\leq p^*\), zero value gap is \(p^*=d^*\), and strong duality means zero value gap, with attainment stated separately whenever required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal value is the infimum of the primal objective over its feasible set, and the dual value is the supremum of the dual objective over its feasible set. For finite values, their difference is the value duality gap. Attainment means that a feasible point realizes the relevant infimum or supremum. Weak duality, equality of values, primal attainment, and dual attainment are distinct predicates.
assumptions_latex: \((P)\) is oriented as a minimization problem and \((D)\) as a maximization problem.
The numerical gap \(\Delta^*\) is used only when \(p^*,d^*\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The value relation is classified by \(d^*\leq p^*\), the gap \(\Delta^*=p^*-d^*\), and the two independent attainment predicates.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For finite values, zero gap is \(\Delta^*=0\).
Primal attainment is equivalent to existence of \(x^*\in X\) with \(f(x^*)=p^*\), and dual attainment is analogous.
special_cases_latex: If feasible \(x^*,y^*\) satisfy \(f(x^*)=g(y^*)\) under weak duality, both values are attained and equal.
immediate_consequences_latex: Value equality alone does not imply that either optimal value is attained.
Attainment on one side does not by itself imply attainment on the other side.
boundary_notes: Expressions such as \(+\infty-+\infty\) or \(-\infty-(-\infty)\) are not numerical gaps.
Some literature includes one-sided or two-sided attainment in its definition of strong duality; this record keeps those predicates explicit.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak-Duality Property
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((P)\) minimize \(f(x)\) over \(x\in X\), and let \((D)\) maximize \(g(y)\) over \(y\in Y\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of the weak-duality relation for a minimization primal and maximization dual; no regularity or attainment hypothesis is included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The pair \((P),(D)\) satisfies weak duality when \[g(y)\leq f(x)\qquad\forall x\in X,\ \forall y\in Y.\] Consequently, in the extended-real order, \[d^*:=\sup_{y\in Y}g(y)\leq p^*:=\inf_{x\in X}f(x).\] For the conic pair \(f(x)=c^Tx\), \(g(y)=b^Ty\), \(Ax-b\in K\), \(A^Ty=c\), and \(y\in K^*\), the pointwise inequality is \[c^Tx-b^Ty=\langle y,Ax-b\rangle\geq0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak duality means that every feasible dual objective is no larger than every feasible primal objective. Therefore the dual supremum is no larger than the primal infimum. In conic programming, the difference between the two feasible objective values is the pairing of the primal slack with the dual-cone multiplier, which is nonnegative by their cone memberships.
assumptions_latex: \((P)\) is a minimization problem and \((D)\) is a maximization problem.
For the conic formula, \(Ax-b\in K\), \(y\in K^*\), and \(A^Ty=c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(y)\leq f(x)\) for every feasible pair, and hence \(d^*\leq p^*\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Every dual-feasible point defines a valid lower bound on every primal-feasible objective value.
For finite values, weak duality is equivalent to \(p^*-d^*\geq0\).
special_cases_latex: In LP, the feasible-pair gap is \(y^T(Ax-b)\geq0\) with both vectors componentwise nonnegative.
In SDP, the gap is \(\operatorname{tr}(YS)\geq0\) for \(Y,S\succeq0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A feasible pair with equal objective values is primal–dual optimal.
A dual-feasible objective value is an independently checkable lower bound for a primal minimization problem.
boundary_notes: Weak duality does not assert equality of values, feasibility, finiteness, or attainment.
For a maximization primal and minimization dual, the bound orientation is reversed.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Value-function conjugacy and perturbational weak duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies the conjugate of a marginal value function and derives the associated weak-duality inequality without convexity, closedness, or properness assumptions on the perturbation function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathcal H\times\mathcal K\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and let \(\vartheta(y)=\inf_{x\in\mathcal H}F(x,y)\). Then
\[
\vartheta^*(v)=F^*(0,v)\quad(\forall v\in\mathcal K),
\]
and
\[
-\inf_{v\in\mathcal K}F^*(0,v)=\vartheta^{**}(0)\leq\vartheta(0)=\inf_{x\in\mathcal H}F(x,0).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conjugate of the marginal value function is the restriction of the perturbation function's conjugate to a zero first coordinate. Consequently, the negative dual infimum equals the biconjugate value at zero and does not exceed the primal infimum.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) and \(\mathcal K\) are Hilbert spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\vartheta^*=F^*(0,\cdot)\) and \(-\inf F^*(0,\mathcal K)=\vartheta^{**}(0)\leq\vartheta(0)=\inf F(\mathcal H,0)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The ordering requires neither convexity nor a constraint qualification. The dual supremum is taken over nonnegative multipliers for which the dual function is greater than negative infinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f,g_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}, i=1,\ldots,m, and define f^*=\inf\{f(x):g_i(x)\leq 0\ \text{for all }i\}. knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a primal minimization problem and its Lagrange dual maximization problem, weak duality has the orientation
\[
g(y)\le d^*\le p^*\le f(x)
\]
for every primal-feasible \(x\) and dual-feasible \(y\). Thus each dual-feasible point supplies a lower bound on the primal infimum, while each primal-feasible point supplies an upper bound. If the primal is instead posed as a maximization problem with a dual minimization problem, the orientation reverses: primal-feasible values are lower bounds and dual-feasible values are upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For primal minimization, dual feasible values are lower bounds and primal feasible values are upper bounds; the directions reverse for primal maximization.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lower- and Upper-Bound Dual Orientations
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let a primal optimization problem have feasible set \(X\) and objective \(f\), and let a dual problem have feasible set \(Y\) and objective \(g\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Both conventional orientations are covered explicitly; all comparisons are between feasible objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the min-primal/max-dual orientation, weak dual bounds satisfy \[g(y)\leq f(x)\quad\forall(x,y)\in X\times Y,\qquad \sup_{y\in Y}g(y)\leq\inf_{x\in X}f(x),\] so dual-feasible points give lower bounds. In the max-primal/min-dual orientation, weak dual bounds satisfy \[f(x)\leq g(y)\quad\forall(x,y)\in X\times Y,\qquad \sup_{x\in X}f(x)\leq\inf_{y\in Y}g(y),\] so dual-feasible points give upper bounds. A dual-bound orientation is the chosen one of these two paired order conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a minimization primal with a maximization dual, every dual-feasible value is a lower bound on every primal-feasible value. For a maximization primal with a minimization dual, every dual-feasible value is an upper bound. The term dual bound is therefore incomplete unless the primal and dual optimization orientations are stated.
assumptions_latex: The primal and dual feasible sets and objective directions are specified.
The pointwise feasible-pair inequality holds in the selected orientation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Min/max duality produces certified lower bounds, whereas max/min duality produces certified upper bounds.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Negating both objectives transforms the min/max convention into the max/min convention.
The two conventions express the same order principle after exchanging infimum with negative supremum.
special_cases_latex: A lower-bound certificate \(L\) for \(\inf f\) becomes the upper-bound certificate \(-L\) for \(\sup(-f)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The sign of a reported primal–dual gap must match the chosen orientation.
Feasible dual values can be compared with incumbent primal values to form one-sided optimality intervals.
boundary_notes: Mixing formulas from opposite orientations can reverse a valid bound.
Extended-real infeasibility conventions must be handled before interpreting a numerical bound.

notation.meaning: Primal value under minimization or maximization orientation.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given feasible \(x\in P\) and \(y\in D\), the computable gap \(G(x,y)=f(x)-g(y)\) is nonnegative and certifies
\[
0\le f(x)-p^*\le G(x,y),
\qquad
0\le p^*-g(y)\le G(x,y).
\]
Therefore \(G(x,y)\le\varepsilon\) is a verifiable certificate that \(x\) is \(\varepsilon\)-optimal in objective value and that \(g(y)\) approximates \(p^*\) within \(\varepsilon\). The certificate uses only primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and evaluation of the two objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible primal-dual pair with gap at most epsilon certifies that each objective value lies within epsilon of the primal optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak-Duality Certification

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relative Weak-Duality Gap Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative primal-objective certification when the dual bound is strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in P\) and \(y\in D\) be feasible and suppose \(0<g(y)\le p^*\le f(x)\). Then
\[
0\le \frac{f(x)-p^*}{p^*}\le \frac{f(x)-g(y)}{g(y)}.
\]
Consequently, \(f(x)-g(y)\le\varepsilon g(y)\) implies \(f(x)\le(1+\varepsilon)p^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly positive dual lower bound converts the absolute primal–dual gap into a relative primal-suboptimality certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in P\) and \(y\in D\) are primal and dual feasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Relative Weak-Duality Gap Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasible-Pair Weak-Duality Certificate
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((P)\) minimize \(f\) over \(X\), let \((D)\) maximize \(g\) over \(Y\), and assume weak duality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic exact feasibility certificates and their finite-gap quality measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A weak-duality certificate is a dual-feasible point \(\hat y\in Y\) together with its certified bound \(L:=g(\hat y)\), satisfying \[L\leq f(x)\qquad\forall x\in X.\] If a primal-feasible point \(\hat x\in X\) is also supplied, the certificate interval is \[g(\hat y)\leq p^*\leq f(\hat x),\] and its primal–dual certificate gap is \[G(\hat x,\hat y):=f(\hat x)-g(\hat y)\geq0.\] The pair is an \(\varepsilon\)-certificate when \(G(\hat x,\hat y)\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual-feasible point certifies a global lower bound for a primal minimization problem. When a primal-feasible point is also available, the two objective values bracket the unknown optimum. Their nonnegative difference is the certificate gap. If that difference is at most a prescribed tolerance, the pair certifies that the primal point and dual bound are each within that tolerance of the common bracketed value.
assumptions_latex: Weak duality holds: \(g(y)\leq f(x)\) for all feasible \(x,y\).
For an \(\varepsilon\)-certificate, \(\hat x\in X\), \(\hat y\in Y\), and \(\varepsilon\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(\hat y)\leq p^*\leq f(\hat x)\), and \(G(\hat x,\hat y)\leq\varepsilon\) certifies an objective bracket of width at most \(\varepsilon\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(f(\hat x)-p^*\leq G(\hat x,\hat y)\) and \(p^*-g(\hat y)\leq G(\hat x,\hat y)\).
A zero-gap feasible pair is an exact primal–dual optimality certificate.
special_cases_latex: For a conic pair, \(G(x,y)=\langle y,Ax-b\rangle\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Either endpoint of the certificate interval is a valid one-sided bound.
A sequence of feasible pairs with gaps converging to zero yields converging objective brackets, even if limit points are not asserted.
boundary_notes: Small objective gap does not certify feasibility when the displayed points are only approximately feasible.
A certificate gap is attached to a feasible pair and differs from the optimal-value gap when the pair is suboptimal.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gap–Attainment Regime Classification
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(p^*:=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\) and \(d^*:=\sup_{y\in Y}g(y)\) be finite values satisfying \(d^*\leq p^*\). Let \(X^*:=\{x\in X:f(x)=p^*\}\) and \(Y^*:=\{y\in Y:g(y)=d^*\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-valued min-primal/max-dual pairs under weak duality; infeasibility and infinite values are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The duality-gap attainment regime is the tuple \[\mathcal R:=\bigl(\Delta^*,\mathbf 1_{X^*\neq\varnothing},\mathbf 1_{Y^*\neq\varnothing}\bigr),\qquad \Delta^*:=p^*-d^*\geq0.\] Its gap component is either zero or positive, while each attainment component records whether the corresponding extremum is realized. Thus zero gap and positive gap each admit four formal attainment patterns: both sides attain, only the primal attains, only the dual attains, or neither side attains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finite primal and dual values under weak duality, a regime is specified by the numerical optimal-value gap and two independent indicators recording primal and dual attainment. Equality of values does not determine attainment, and attainment does not determine equality of values. The classification therefore retains all three pieces of information rather than collapsing them into a single strong-duality label.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every finite-valued pair belongs to exactly one tuple \((\Delta^*,a_P,a_D)\in[0,\infty)\times\{0,1\}^2\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(a_P=1\iff X^*\neq\varnothing\), and \(a_D=1\iff Y^*\neq\varnothing\).
Zero gap with two-sided attainment is \((0,1,1)\); zero gap without any attainment is \((0,0,0)\).
special_cases_latex: Under a conic Slater condition on the primal and boundedness below, the dual attains and \(\Delta^*=0\), while primal attainment requires a separate conclusion.
If both conic problems are strictly feasible, the standard conic-duality theorem gives \((0,1,1)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The predicates \(\Delta^*=0\), \(X^*\neq\varnothing\), and \(Y^*\neq\varnothing\) must be checked separately.
A zero-gap feasible pair immediately places the problem in regime \((0,1,1)\).
boundary_notes: The tuple does not encode infeasibility, unboundedness, or undefined extended-real differences.
Some formal combinations may be ruled out for particular problem classes by stronger duality theorems.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Positive Optimal-Value Gap
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((P),(D)\) be a min-primal/max-dual pair with finite values \(p^*,d^*\in\mathbb R\) satisfying weak duality \(d^*\leq p^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite positive gaps only; infeasible sides and infinite or undefined gaps are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The pair is in a nonzero duality-gap regime when \[\Delta^*:=p^*-d^*>0.\] Its attainment subtype is determined independently by \[a_P:=\mathbf1_{\operatorname{Argmin}P\neq\varnothing},\qquad a_D:=\mathbf1_{\operatorname{Argmax}D\neq\varnothing}.\] Hence a finite nonzero-gap regime is recorded as \((\Delta^*,a_P,a_D)\in(0,\infty)\times\{0,1\}^2\). No primal-feasible and dual-feasible pair can have equal objectives in this regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero duality-gap regime occurs when both optimal values are finite and the primal infimum strictly exceeds the dual supremum. Whether either extremum is attained is separate, so positive-gap problems may be classified by primal and dual attainment indicators. Because every feasible primal objective is at least the primal value and every feasible dual objective is at most the dual value, equal feasible objective values are impossible when the optimal-value gap is positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta^*\in(0,\infty)\), with attainment subtype \((a_P,a_D)\in\{0,1\}^2\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A primal-dual pair has a positive finite duality gap when both optimal values are finite and

Equivalently, weak duality is strict at the level of optimal values: every dual-feasible objective is bounded above by \(d^*\), every primal-feasible objective is bounded below by \(p^*\), and these best bounds remain separated by the finite amount \(\Delta\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: One- or Two-Sided Nonattainment
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(p^*:=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\) and \(d^*:=\sup_{y\in Y}g(y)\) be finite values for a min-primal/max-dual pair.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-valued problems; nonattainment is distinguished from infeasibility and unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Primal nonattainment means \[X\neq\varnothing,\quad p^*\in\mathbb R,\quad \{x\in X:f(x)=p^*\}=\varnothing.\] Dual nonattainment means \[Y\neq\varnothing,\quad d^*\in\mathbb R,\quad \{y\in Y:g(y)=d^*\}=\varnothing.\] The primal–dual nonattainment regime is specified by which of these predicates holds: primal-only, dual-only, or two-sided nonattainment. Each may coexist with zero gap \(p^*=d^*\) or, when allowed by the problem class, with a finite positive gap \(p^*>d^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite primal value is not attained when the primal feasible set is nonempty but no feasible point realizes its infimum. Dual nonattainment is defined analogously for a finite supremum. The combined regime records whether nonattainment occurs only on the primal side, only on the dual side, or on both. This classification is independent of whether the two finite values are equal.
assumptions_latex: The relevant feasible set is nonempty.
The relevant optimal value is finite.
No feasible point realizes the relevant infimum or supremum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nonattainment is the emptiness of the optimizer set despite nonempty feasibility and a finite extremal value, classified separately on the primal and dual sides.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Primal nonattainment means every \(x\in X\) satisfies \(f(x)>p^*\), while a sequence \((x_k)\subseteq X\) exists with \(f(x_k)\to p^*\).
Dual nonattainment means every \(y\in Y\) satisfies \(g(y)<d^*\), while a sequence \((y_k)\subseteq Y\) exists with \(g(y_k)\to d^*\).
special_cases_latex: A strictly feasible, bounded conic primal can fail to attain its infimum even though its dual attains the same value; this is primal-only nonattainment with zero gap.
When both primal and dual strictly satisfy the hypotheses of the standard conic-duality corollary, two-sided attainment holds and all nonattainment regimes are excluded.
immediate_consequences_latex: A finite-valued nonattained problem has optimizing sequences but no optimizer.
Zero value gap does not by itself produce a feasible zero-gap pair if either side fails to attain.
boundary_notes: An empty feasible set is infeasibility, not nonattainment under this definition.
An objective diverging to \(-\infty\) in a minimization problem or \(+\infty\) in a maximization problem is unboundedness, not finite nonattainment.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong duality for a primal–dual pair
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P\) be a minimization problem with extended-real optimal value \(p^*=\inf_{x\in X}F(x)\), and let \(D\) be a maximization dual with value \(d^*=\sup_{y\in Y}G(y)\). The dual construction is assumed to satisfy weak duality: \(G(y)\leq F(x)\) for every primal-feasible \(x\) and dual-feasible \(y\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition concerns equality of optimal values. It does not by itself assert feasibility, finiteness, attainment, existence of multipliers, or validity of any particular constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\text{Strong duality holds for }(P,D)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad p^*=d^*.\] A strong-duality theorem family is a collection of results giving explicit hypotheses under which this equality holds, possibly together with separately stated primal or dual attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong duality means that the primal infimum and dual supremum are equal. A strong-duality theorem additionally specifies hypotheses that guarantee this equality; attainment and finiteness are separate assertions unless explicitly included.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If both values are finite, strong duality is equivalent to vanishing optimal duality gap: \[p^*-d^*=0.\]
If the dual value is written as \(q^*=\sup_y q(y)\), the same definition is \[\inf_{x\in X}F(x)=\sup_{y\in Y}q(y).\]
special_cases_latex: For a Lagrangian dual, \(q(y)=\inf_x L(x,y)\), so strong duality is \[\inf_{x\text{ feasible}}F(x)=\sup_{y\text{ dual feasible}}\inf_x L(x,y).\]
Fenchel and conic duality are members of this family after their associated primal and dual value functions are specified.
immediate_consequences_latex: If feasible points \(\bar x,\bar y\) satisfy \(F(\bar x)=G(\bar y)\), weak duality makes both optimal and establishes strong duality.
Strong duality alone permits nonattainment on either side; equality of two unattained finite values still satisfies the definition.
boundary_notes: The equality is interpreted in the extended-real sense only when the adopted duality framework makes that comparison meaningful.
Some authors use “strong duality” for equality plus dual attainment. This record reserves attainment for an additional conclusion.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong duality from lower semicontinuity of the value function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A perturbational strong-duality condition asserting equality of finite primal and dual values, without asserting attainment of either infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H\oplus\mathcal K)\), and let \(\vartheta(y)=\inf_{x\in\mathcal H}F(x,y)\). If \(\vartheta\) is lower semicontinuous at \(0\) and \(\vartheta(0)\in\mathbb R\), then
\[
\inf_{x\in\mathcal H}F(x,0)=-\inf_{v\in\mathcal K}F^*(0,v)\in\mathbb R.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper lower-semicontinuous convex perturbation function, lower semicontinuity and finiteness of its value function at zero guarantee equality of the finite primal and dual values. Dual or primal attainment is not asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in\mathcal H}F(x,0)=-\inf_{v\in\mathcal K}F^*(0,v)\in\mathbb R\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong duality and value-function sensitivity under continuity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbational convex duality identifying dual solutions with value-function subgradients, with additional Banach-space compactness and directional-differentiability conclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\varphi:X\times U\to\overline{\mathbb R}$ be proper and convex, and suppose that $v(\bar u)=\operatorname{val}(P_{\bar u})$ is finite and that $v$ is continuous at $\bar u\in U$. Then $\operatorname{val}(P_{\bar u})=\operatorname{val}(D_{\bar u})$, $\mathcal S(D_{\bar u})=\partial v(\bar u)\ne\varnothing$, and $[\mathcal S(D_{\bar u})]^\infty=\{0\}$. If, additionally, $U$ is a Banach space with its strong topology, then $\mathcal S(D_{\bar u})$ is convex, bounded, and weak-* compact in $U^*$, $v$ is Hadamard directionally differentiable at $\bar u$, and $v'(\bar u;d)=\sup_{u^*\in\mathcal S(D_{\bar u})}\langle u^*,d\rangle$ for every $d\in U$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuity and finiteness of the convex value function at the reference parameter imply strong duality and identify the nonempty dual solution set with the value-function subdifferential; this set has trivial recession cone. For a strongly topologized Banach parameter space, the dual solution set is also bounded and weak-star compact, and its support function gives the Hadamard directional derivative of the value function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{val}(P_{\bar u})=\operatorname{val}(D_{\bar u}),\quad \mathcal S(D_{\bar u})=\partial v(\bar u)\ne\varnothing,\quad [\mathcal S(D_{\bar u})]^\infty=\{0\};\quad U\text{ Banach}\Longrightarrow v'(\bar u;d)=\sup_{u^*\in\mathcal S(D_{\bar u})}\langle u^*,d\rangle.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex inequality-constrained programming under either strict feasibility or affine-constraint relative-interior feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be convex, let \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_r\) be convex, and suppose \(f^*\in\mathbb R\). Assume either (i) \(\exists\bar x\in X\) with \(g_j(\bar x)<0\) for every \(j\), or (ii) every \(g_j\) is affine and \(\exists\bar x\in\operatorname{ri}(X)\) with \(g(\bar x)\le0\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Lagrangian duality and constraint qualifications
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines strong duality for a primal problem and its Lagrange dual while distinguishing convexity from sufficient regularity conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Strong Lagrangian duality holds when \[d^\star=p^\star.\] Thus the best lower bound furnished by the Lagrange dual function is tight; whenever the difference \(p^\star-d^\star\) is defined, this is equivalent to a zero optimal duality gap. For a convex problem \[\min_x f_0(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad f_i(x)\le0\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\quad Ax=b,\] with convex \(f_0,\ldots,f_m\), convexity alone does not always guarantee strong duality. Additional conditions that guarantee it are called constraint qualifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong Lagrangian duality means equality of the primal and dual optimal values, so the dual lower bound is tight. For a defined duality gap, this is equivalent to the gap being zero. knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=e^x\), \(g(z)=0\), and \(A=0\) on one-dimensional Euclidean spaces. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fenchel sum primal–dual pair and duality gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions of the primal and dual minimization problems, their extended optimal values, and the exceptional convention used when signed value equality occurs at infinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For proper \(f,g:\mathcal H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), the primal problem is \[\operatorname*{minimize}_{x\in\mathcal H}\;f(x)+g(x),\] and its dual problem is \[\operatorname*{minimize}_{u\in\mathcal H}\;f^*(-u)+g^*(u).\] Set \[\mu=\inf_{x\in\mathcal H}(f(x)+g(x)),\qquad \mu^*=\inf_{u\in\mathcal H}(f^*(-u)+g^*(u)).\] The duality gap is \[\Delta(f,g)=\begin{cases}0,&\mu=-\mu^*\in\{-\infty,+\infty\},\\ \mu+\mu^*,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal minimizes the sum of the functions, while the dual minimizes the sum of their conjugates with a sign reversal in the first argument. The gap is the sum of their optimal values, except that it is defined as zero when the primal value equals the signed dual value at infinity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mu:=\inf_{x\in\mathcal H}(f+g)(x)\), \(\mu^*:=\inf_{u\in\mathcal H}(f^*(-u)+g^*(u))\), and \(\Delta(f,g)=0\) if \(\mu=-\mu^*\in\{-\infty,+\infty\}\), while \(\Delta(f,g)=\mu+\mu^*\) otherwise.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[
p^\star=\inf\{\langle c,x\rangle:x\in K,\ Ax-b\in C\},
\qquad
d^\star=\sup\{\langle b,y\rangle:y\in C^*,\ c-A^*y\in K^*\},

Then \(p^\star=d^\star\), and the primal infimum is attained.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conic primal–dual strong duality
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, let \(K\subseteq E\) be a nonempty closed convex cone, and let \(f:E\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex. Set \(K^*=\{y:\langle y,x\rangle\geq0\ \forall x\in K\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is the conjugate conic pair obtained by minimizing a closed convex function over a cone. Linear conic programming is a specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[p^*=\inf_{x\in K}f(x),\qquad d^*=\sup_{y\in K^*}\bigl(-f^*(y)\bigr).\] \[\text{Conic strong duality holds}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad p^*=d^*.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimization of a closed proper convex function over a closed convex cone, the conjugate dual maximizes the negative conjugate over the dual cone. Conic strong duality means equality of those two optimal values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\inf_{x\in K}f(x)=-\inf_{y\in K^*}f^*(y).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Using the polar cone \(K^\circ=\{y:\langle y,x\rangle\leq0\ \forall x\in K\}\), one may write the dual variable as \(-y\in K^\circ\).
The formulation follows from Fenchel duality by writing the primal objective as \(f+\iota_K\), since \(\iota_K^*\) is the support function of \(K\).
special_cases_latex: For \(f(x)=\langle c,x\rangle+\iota_{\{x:Ax=b\}}(x)\), the pair reduces to the usual linear conic primal and dual.
Choosing \(K\) as a nonnegative orthant, second-order cone, or positive-semidefinite cone gives linear, second-order-cone, or semidefinite duality.
immediate_consequences_latex: A relative-interior qualification can guarantee both zero duality gap and dual attainment when the primal value is finite.
The dual cone is closed and convex even if the original cone is not assumed self-dual.
boundary_notes: The sign of the dual cone depends on whether a source uses a polar or positive-dual convention.
Strong duality is distinct from strict feasibility and from complementary slackness.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: One-Sided Slater Does Not Ensure Same-Side Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp attainment boundary for the primal-Slater form of conic strong duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
K=\{(u,v,t)\in\mathbb R^3: u\ge0,\ v\ge0,\ 2uv\ge t^2\}
\]
be the rotated second-order cone, and consider
\[
\inf\{v:(u,v,t)\in K,\ t=1\}.
\]
The point \((1,1,1)\) is strictly feasible because \(2>1\). The infimum equals \(0\), since \((u,v,t)=(1/(2\varepsilon),\varepsilon,1)\) is feasible for every \(\varepsilon>0\), but no feasible point has \(v=0\). Thus primal conic Slater and a finite primal value do not imply primal attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rotated-cone program can be strictly primal feasible with finite but unattained primal infimum, so primal Slater guarantees opposite-side attainment only.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is the displayed closed convex rotated second-order cone.
The equality constraint is \(t=1\) and the objective is \(v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^\star=0\) is finite but is not attained, despite primal strict feasibility.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cone-Programming Strong Duality and One-Sided Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternative primal-side and dual-side constraint qualifications for strong duality and opposite-side attainment in a cone-programming pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) and \(K\) be convex cones in the cone-programming pair, with optimal values \(p\) and \(d\). (a) If \(b\in\operatorname{int}(AK-H)\), or \(b\in AK-\operatorname{int}H\), or \(b\in A(\operatorname{int}K)-H\) and either \(H\) is polyhedral or \(A\) is surjective, then \(p=d\), and the dual optimal value is attained whenever \(d\) is finite. (b) If \(H\) and \(K\) are closed and \(-c\in\operatorname{int}(A^*H^-+K^-)\), or \(-c\in A^*H^-+\operatorname{int}(K^-)\), or \(-c\in A^*(\operatorname{int}(H^-))+K^-\) and either \(K\) is polyhedral or \(A^*\) is surjective, then \(p=d\), and the primal optimal value is attained whenever \(p\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For convex cone programs, any listed primal-side interiority condition gives zero duality gap and attainment of a finite dual optimum. Independently, when both cones are closed, any listed dual-side interiority condition gives zero duality gap and attainment of a finite primal optimum. The polyhedrality-or-surjectivity qualification applies only to the third condition in each list.
assumptions_latex: \text{For part (a), }b\in\operatorname{int}(AK-H)\;\lor\;b\in AK-\operatorname{int}H\;\lor\;\bigl(b\in A(\operatorname{int}K)-H\land(H\text{ is polyhedral}\lor A\text{ is surjective})\bigr)

\text{For part (b), }H,K\text{ are closed and }-c\in\operatorname{int}(A^*H^-+K^-)\;\lor\;-c\in A^*H^-+\operatorname{int}(K^-)\;\lor\;\bigl(-c\in A^*(\operatorname{int}(H^-))+K^-\land(K\text{ is polyhedral}\lor A^*\text{ is surjective})\bigr)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Under a part (a) condition, }p=d\text{ and finite }d\text{ is attained};\qquad \text{under a part (b) condition, }p=d\text{ and finite }p\text{ is attained}.
