knowledge_statements.statement_title: Instability of a Normalized Certificate Mapping
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(D\) and \(Y\) be normed spaces, let \(\mathcal D\subseteq D\) be a parameterized family of optimization or feasibility instances, and let \(\mathcal C(d)\subseteq Y\) be the set of dual certificates for instance \(d\). When certificates are invariant under positive scaling, fix a continuous positive normalization \(n:Y\to\mathbb R_+\) and set \(\widehat{\mathcal C}(d)=\{y\in\mathcal C(d):n(y)=1\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition concerns topological instability of finite-valued dual certificates under deterministic perturbations. It does not assert that every duality failure has this form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The certificate system is unstable at \(\bar d\in\mathcal D\) if the normalized set-valued map \(\widehat{\mathcal C}\) is not outer semicontinuous at \(\bar d\), or is not locally bounded there. Explicitly, instability holds when at least one of the following occurs: \[\exists d_k\to\bar d,\ \exists y_k\in\widehat{\mathcal C}(d_k),\ y_k\to\bar y,\quad \bar y\notin\widehat{\mathcal C}(\bar d),\] or \[\exists d_k\to\bar d,\ \exists y_k\in\widehat{\mathcal C}(d_k),\quad \|y_k\|\to+\infty.\] If no scale invariance is present, the same conditions apply directly to \(\mathcal C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate pathology is unstable at a reference instance when arbitrarily small data perturbations admit certificates whose finite limits cease to be certificates at the reference instance, or when certificates cannot be kept uniformly bounded near that instance. Homogeneous certificates are first restricted to a fixed normalization so that trivial rescaling is not mistaken for instability.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C(d)\) is the certificate set associated with the instance \(d\).
If \(\mathcal C(d)\) is positively homogeneous, the normalization satisfies \(n(y)>0\) on every nonzero certificate ray under consideration.
Convergence and boundedness are taken in the specified norm topologies of \(D\) and \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar d\) exhibits unstable-certificate pathology exactly when \(\widehat{\mathcal C}\) fails outer semicontinuity or local boundedness at \(\bar d\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: In metric spaces, outer semicontinuity is equivalent to \(\limsup_{d\to\bar d}\widehat{\mathcal C}(d)\subseteq\widehat{\mathcal C}(\bar d)\); instability includes failure of this inclusion.
Local boundedness fails precisely when every neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar d\) has \(\bigcup_{d\in U}\widehat{\mathcal C}(d)\) unbounded.
special_cases_latex: For multiplier sets, one may take \(\mathcal C(d)\) to be the set of KKT multipliers and omit normalization when stationarity fixes their scale.
For homogeneous infeasibility certificates, a common normalization is \(n(y)=\|y\|\) or a fixed affine base condition.
immediate_consequences_latex: A locally bounded, outer-semicontinuous certificate mapping cannot exhibit either defining instability sequence.
The definition separates disappearance of limiting certificates from norm blow-up; either phenomenon is sufficient.
boundary_notes: Nonuniqueness alone is not instability: a locally bounded outer-semicontinuous set-valued certificate map may have many values.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Interior Finiteness Prevents Local Subgradient Blow-Up
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional sufficient condition excluding the local-unboundedness branch of certificate instability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(v:\mathbb R^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex. If \(v\) is finite on an open neighborhood of \(0\), then for every compact set \(K\subset\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}v)\),
\[
\bigcup_{u\in K}\partial v(u)
\]
is bounded. In particular, there are a neighborhood \(V\) of \(0\) and \(M<+\infty\) such that \(\|\lambda\|\le M\) for every \(u\in V\) and \(\lambda\in\partial v(u)\). Hence multiplier blow-up under \(u\to0\) requires failure of local finiteness or of the subgradient representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-dimensional convex value function that is finite near the reference perturbation has locally bounded supporting multipliers, so certificate blow-up can occur only at a domain or representation boundary.
assumptions_latex: \(v\) is finite on an open neighborhood of \(0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists V\ni0,\ M<+\infty:\ \sup\{\|\lambda\|:u\in V,\lambda\in\partial v(u)\}\le M.
knowledge_statements.title: Interior Finiteness Prevents Local Subgradient Blow-Up

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Open-Ray Weak-Infeasibility Example
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional infeasible membership system with no strict finite linear separator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C=(0,+\infty)\subset\mathbb R\) and \(b=0\). Then \(b\notin C\) but \(b\in\overline C\). For every \(y\in\mathbb R\),
\[
\sup_{c\in C}yc\ge 0=yb;
\]
the supremum is \(+\infty\) when \(y>0\) and \(0\) when \(y\le0\). Hence no \(y\) satisfies \(\sup_{c\in C}yc<yb\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero is outside the open positive ray but lies in its closure, so no finite linear functional strictly separates it from that attainable set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b\notin C,\qquad \nexists y\in\mathbb R:\ \sup_{c\in C}yc<yb.

notation.meaning: infeasible target in the closure of the attainable set

assumptions_latex: The continuous linear image associated with a convex feasibility system is a convex set \(C\) in a topological vector space \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The system \(b\in C\) is infeasible, but no continuous linear functional strictly separates \(b\) from \(C\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak infeasibility caused by a target in a nonclosed attainable set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Since \(b\notin C\), the membership system \(b\in C\) is infeasible. Yet \(b\in\overline C\) implies that every continuous \(y^*\in Y^*\) satisfies
\[\langle y^*,b\rangle\leq\sup_{c\in C}\langle y^*,c\rangle.\]
Therefore no finite continuous certificate can satisfy
\[\sup_{c\in C}\langle y^*,c\rangle<\langle y^*,b\rangle,\]
which would strongly separate the target from the attainable set. Thus nonclosedness produces weak infeasibility: infeasibility is real, but every finite linear separating certificate fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If an infeasible target lies in the closure of the attainable set, continuity prevents every linear functional from strictly separating it, so no finite separation certificate exists.
knowledge_statements.title: Absence of Finite Separating Certificates

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Infeasibility Without a Continuous Strict Separator
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be Hausdorff locally convex spaces, let \(A:X\to Y\) be continuous linear, let \(K\subseteq Y\) be a closed convex cone, and let \(b\in Y\). Consider the conic system \(Ax-b\in K\). Its continuous dual cone is \(K^*=\{y^*\in Y^*: \langle y^*,k\rangle\ge0\ \forall k\in K\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition covers weakly infeasible conic systems in a specified locally convex topology. A certificate is finite when it is an ordinary continuous functional, not a limiting or extended-valued object.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The system has an absence of finite separating certificates when \[b\notin A(X)-K\] but there is no \(y^*\in Y^*\) satisfying \[y^*\in K^*,\qquad A^*y^*=0,\qquad \langle y^*,b\rangle>0.\] A canonical sufficient geometric realization of this pathology is \[b\in\overline{A(X)-K}\setminus\bigl(A(X)-K\bigr),\] where closure is taken in the chosen topology of \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conic system is infeasible without a finite separating certificate when the right-hand side is outside the attainable cone-shift set, yet no continuous dual functional annihilating the range of the linear map and nonnegative on the cone strictly separates the right-hand side. The characteristic weak-infeasibility case places the right-hand side in the closure of the attainable set but not in the set itself.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone in \(Y\).
Only continuous linear functionals in \(Y^*\) count as finite separating certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax-b\in K\) is infeasible, while \(\{y^*\in K^*:A^*y^*=0,\ \langle y^*,b\rangle>0\}=\varnothing\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(S=A(X)-K\), a finite certificate is a continuous functional \(y^*\) with \(\sup_{s\in S}\langle y^*,s\rangle\le0<\langle y^*,b\rangle\).
If \(b\in\overline S\setminus S\), no continuous functional can strictly separate \(b\) from \(S\).
special_cases_latex: In finite-dimensional conic optimization, nonclosedness of \(A(X)-K\) permits infeasibility with zero distance to feasibility.
For semidefinite systems, this definition captures weak infeasibility when no finite Farkas-type matrix certificate exists.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every neighborhood of \(b\) intersects \(A(X)-K\) in the closure-boundary case.
Any usable certificate must then arise from a reformulation, facial reduction, an extended dual, or a limiting construction.
boundary_notes: Strong infeasibility, where \(b\notin\overline{A(X)-K}\), is excluded from the canonical closure-boundary case.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relative-Interior versus Strong-Relative-Interior Boundary
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space and let \(f,g\in\Gamma_0(H)\). Put \(D=\operatorname{dom}f-\operatorname{dom}g\). Define \(\operatorname{sri}D=\{z\in D:\operatorname{cone}(D-z)=\overline{\operatorname{span}}(D-z)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition isolates a qualification boundary that disappears in finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces but can be genuine in infinite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The pair \((f,g)\) lies on the finite–infinite dimensional duality boundary when \[0\in\operatorname{ri}D\setminus\operatorname{sri}D,\qquad D=\operatorname{dom}f-\operatorname{dom}g.\] Equivalently, \(\operatorname{cone}D\) is a linear subspace but is not closed. In finite dimension, \(\operatorname{sri}D=\operatorname{ri}D\), so this boundary set is empty; in infinite dimension it may be nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The boundary occurs when the ordinary relative-interior qualification holds but the strong-relative-interior qualification fails. Geometrically, the cone generated by the domain difference is a nonclosed linear subspace. Finite-dimensional spaces identify relative and strong relative interiors, whereas infinite-dimensional spaces need not.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\operatorname{ri}D\setminus\operatorname{sri}D\), equivalently \(\operatorname{cone}D\) is linear and nonclosed.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(0\in D\), \(0\in\operatorname{sri}D\) means \(\operatorname{cone}D=\overline{\operatorname{span}}D\).
The boundary condition is equivalent to the relative-interior cone being linear while failing the closed-subspace condition required by the Attouch–Brézis qualification.
special_cases_latex: If \(H\) is finite-dimensional, \(\operatorname{sri}D=\operatorname{ri}D\), so the pathology cannot occur.
If \(U,V\) are closed subspaces of an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space and \(U+V\) is not closed, indicator functions of \(U\) and \(V\) realize the boundary.
immediate_consequences_latex: A finite-dimensional relative-interior qualification cannot automatically be transferred to an infinite-dimensional model.
At this boundary, replacing \(\operatorname{sri}\) by \(\operatorname{ri}\) in exact conjugacy statements is generally invalid.
boundary_notes: The definition does not claim that every infinite-dimensional duality failure is caused by this boundary.
Failure of strong relative interior alone does not determine the size of a duality gap.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A polyhedral cone has a finite generator representation \(K=\operatorname{cone}\{r_1,\ldots,r_m\}\). Hence
\[A(K)=\operatorname{cone}\{Ar_1,\ldots,Ar_m\},\]
which is again polyhedral and therefore closed in finite-dimensional \(Y\). This closed-image regime supports strong separation of every \(b\notin A(K)\). The conclusion cannot be extended to arbitrary closed convex cones: even in finite dimensions, a linear image \(A(K)\), or an affine projection derived from it, can be nonclosed. Thus finite dimensionality supplies strong separation for closed images but does not itself guarantee image closedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear images of polyhedral cones remain polyhedral and closed. General closed convex cones can have nonclosed images even in finite dimensions, so dimensionality alone is insufficient.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed Linear-Image Regimes for Convex Sets
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear. Write \(R_C\) for the recession cone, \(L_C=R_C\cap(-R_C)\) for the lineality space, and \(N(A)\) for the nullspace.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition concerns finite-dimensional sufficient regimes in which the linear image needed by separation and duality arguments is closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The pair \((A,C)\) is in a finite-dimensional closedness regime when \(A(C)\) is closed. Two canonical sufficient regimes are \[C\ \text{polyhedral},\] and \[R_C\cap N(A)\subseteq L_C.\] The stronger condition \(R_C\cap N(A)=\{0\}\) is also sufficient. For sums \(C_1+\cdots+C_p\), the corresponding regime requires that \(d_i\in R_{C_i}\) and \(\sum_i d_i=0\) imply \(d_i\in L_{C_i}\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-dimensional closedness regime is a configuration in which the linear image of a closed convex set is itself closed. Polyhedrality is one such regime. Another excludes nonlineal recession directions that are invisible to the linear map. The analogous condition for Minkowski sums excludes mutually cancelling recession directions except for lineality directions.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
Recession and lineality are computed for the stated closed convex sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under either displayed sufficient regime, \(A(C)\) is closed; under the sum condition, \(C_1+\cdots+C_p\) is closed.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The condition \(R_C\cap N(A)\subseteq L_C\) says that every recession direction lost under projection is reversible within \(C\).
For two sets, a sufficient pointed form is \(R_{C_1}\cap(-R_{C_2})=\{0\}\).
special_cases_latex: The linear image of every polyhedral set is polyhedral and closed.
If \(C\) is bounded, then \(R_C=\{0\}\), so every linear image \(A(C)\) is closed.
If one summand is compact and the other is closed, their Minkowski sum is closed.
immediate_consequences_latex: Closed image sets admit ordinary finite-dimensional strict separation from exterior points.
Closedness prevents closure-only perturbation values at the associated projection step.
boundary_notes: A linear image of a nonpolyhedral closed convex set need not be closed, even in finite dimensions.
The recession condition is sufficient in the stated form; this record does not claim it is necessary in every case.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel–Moreau boundary for Hausdorff locally convex dual pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), define
\[f^*(x^*)=\sup_{x\in X}\{\langle x^*,x\rangle-f(x)\},\qquad f^{**}(x)=\sup_{x^*\in X^*}\{\langle x^*,x\rangle-f^*(x^*)\}.\]
If \(f\) is proper and convex, then \(f^{**}\) is its greatest \(\sigma(X,X^*)\)-lower-semicontinuous convex minorant, and \(f=f^{**}\) if and only if \(f\) is lower semicontinuous for that topology. If local convexity or point separation by \(X^*\) is lost, continuous affine functionals may not determine closed convex sets, so this biconjugate characterization and the associated separation-based duality can fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fenchel biconjugacy characterizes weakly lower-semicontinuous convex functions in a separating locally convex dual pair; without that structure, separation and dual recovery may fail.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Topology-Dependent Duality Boundary in a Locally Convex Pair
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((X,\tau)\) be a Hausdorff locally convex space with continuous dual \(X'=(X,\tau)'\). For \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), define \(f^*(x')=\sup_{x\in X}(\langle x',x\rangle-f(x))\) and \(f^{**}(x)=\sup_{x'\in X'}(\langle x',x\rangle-f^*(x'))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition records the point at which duality depends on the selected topology and its continuous dual. It is not a finite-dimensional norm-duality statement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A convex model lies on the locally convex space duality boundary when its algebraic formulation is fixed but the selected topology changes at least one of the following objects: the continuous dual \(X'\), the lower-semicontinuous hull \(\operatorname{cl}_{\tau}f\), or the separating functionals available for its perturbation epigraph. Formally, for two compatible Hausdorff locally convex topologies \(\tau_1,\tau_2\), the boundary is present if \[(X,\tau_1)'\ne(X,\tau_2)'\quad\text{or}\quad \operatorname{cl}_{\tau_1}f\ne\operatorname{cl}_{\tau_2}f.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally convex duality boundary is reached when changing the locally convex topology, while leaving the algebraic optimization model unchanged, changes the continuous dual, the lower-semicontinuous closure of the objective, or the continuous separators available to dualize the perturbation set.
assumptions_latex: \(\tau_1\) and \(\tau_2\) are Hausdorff locally convex topologies on the same vector space \(X\).
Conjugates are formed only with continuous dual functionals for the chosen topology.
Closure and lower semicontinuity are interpreted in the chosen topology.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dual representation is topology-dependent whenever \((X,\tau_1)'\ne(X,\tau_2)'\) or \(\operatorname{cl}_{\tau_1}f\ne\operatorname{cl}_{\tau_2}f\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a proper convex function, topology dependence can be detected by comparing the corresponding biconjugates formed from the two continuous dual pairs.
For a convex perturbation epigraph, the boundary can be expressed as a difference between the continuous supporting hyperplanes supplied by the two duals.
special_cases_latex: For a Banach space, the norm and weak topologies have the same continuous dual, although their compactness properties differ.
For a dual Banach space, weak-star dualization restricts continuous functionals to those represented by the chosen predual.
immediate_consequences_latex: A dual problem is not fully specified until the primal topology or dual pairing is fixed.
Algebraic separation cannot automatically substitute for continuous separation in a topological duality theorem.
boundary_notes: Different topologies can share the same continuous dual; topology dependence is then not implied solely by their being distinct.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exactness Boundary of a Relaxed Formulation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Z\) be a topological vector space, let \(F\subseteq Z\) be the feasible set of an original minimization problem, let \(R\subseteq Z\) be a relaxation with \(F\subseteq R\), and let \(f:Z\to(-\infty,+\infty]\). Define \(p_F=\inf_{z\in F}f(z)\) and \(p_R=\inf_{z\in R}f(z)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition separates value exactness, optimizer recovery, and topological closure effects. It applies to deterministic minimization formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The formulation–relaxation boundary is the partition determined by \[\Delta_{F,R}=p_F-p_R\in[0,+\infty].\] The relaxation is value-exact when \(\Delta_{F,R}=0\), optimizer-exact when additionally \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in R}f(z)\cap F\ne\varnothing,\] and failure occurs when \(\Delta_{F,R}>0\), or when \(\Delta_{F,R}=0\) but every relaxed minimizer lies outside \(F\). A closure-only boundary occurs when \(R=\overline F\), \(p_R=p_F\), and the infimum is attained in \(R\setminus F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The boundary between a formulation and its relaxation is classified by the difference between their optimal values and by whether a relaxed optimizer can be recovered as an original feasible optimizer. Positive gap is value failure; zero gap without recoverability is optimizer failure; closure-only failure occurs when relaxation adds only limit points but attains the common value at a newly added point.
assumptions_latex: Both problems use the same extended-real objective \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure is present exactly when \(p_F>p_R\), or when \(p_F=p_R\) but \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{R}f\cap F=\varnothing\) while the relaxed argmin is nonempty.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Value exactness is \(\inf_F f=\inf_R f\).
Optimizer exactness is equivalent to the existence of \(z^*\in F\) attaining the relaxed value.
special_cases_latex: If \(R=\overline{\operatorname{conv}}F\) and \(f\) is linear, \(p_R\) is the convex-relaxation bound.
If \(F\) is closed and \(R=F\), both exactness notions are automatic whenever an optimizer exists.
immediate_consequences_latex: A zero numerical gap does not imply recovery of an original feasible optimizer.
Positive \(\Delta_{F,R}\) certifies strict weakening of the optimal value.
boundary_notes: The definition does not prescribe how the relaxation is constructed.
No inspected supplied source states this exact three-way taxonomy.
review_flags: A source supporting the combined value/optimizer/closure taxonomy is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting an affine conic system to the minimal face containing its feasible set preserves feasibility and restores relative strict feasibility.
assumptions_latex: The conic affine system is nonempty and finite-dimensional.
\(F\) is the minimal face of \(K\) containing the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S=F\cap\{x:Ax=b\}\quad\text{and}\quad S\cap\operatorname{ri}F\ne\varnothing.

The equality \(h(x)=0\) is represented by \(h(x)\le 0\) and \(-h(x)\le 0\).

However, strict feasibility of the inequality representation would require simultaneously \(h(x)<0\) and \(-h(x)<0\), which is impossible. Therefore strict feasibility is not invariant under this exact reformulation; failure of its Slater condition alone does not imply a geometric defect in the original feasible set.

Equivalently, every lifted slack lies in a proper face \(G\lneq K\).

Thus the formulation has no Slater point even though the feasible geometry is nonempty and relatively regular within its true affine hull.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Three Degeneracies Induced by Redundancy and Lifting
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let an original feasible set \(F\subseteq X\) be represented by \(Gx=h\) and a lifted conic system \(\widehat F=\{(x,w):\mathcal A x+\mathcal B w-b\in K,\ Gx=h\}\), with \(\pi_X(\widehat F)=F\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is a structural taxonomy of representation degeneracies, not an algorithmic classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A representation is redundancy–lifting degenerate when at least one of the following holds: (i) equation redundancy, \[\exists \lambda\ne0:\ G^*\lambda=0,\quad \langle\lambda,h\rangle=0;\] (ii) lift-kernel degeneracy, \[\exists v\ne0:\ \mathcal Bv=0,\] so lifted variables are nonidentifiable; or (iii) facial degeneracy, when every feasible slack belongs to a proper face \(G_K\lneq K\). The taxonomy records the subset of these three predicates that holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redundancy–lifting degeneracy consists of one or more of three independent defects: linearly dependent equality descriptions, invisible directions in the added variables, and confinement of all conic slacks to a proper face. The degeneracy type is the set of predicates satisfied by the representation.
assumptions_latex: The lifted representation projects exactly to the original feasible set.
All maps are linear and continuous in the chosen finite-dimensional or Hilbert setting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The degeneracy label is \(\mathfrak D\subseteq\{\mathrm{equation},\mathrm{kernel},\mathrm{facial}\}\), containing exactly the displayed predicates that hold.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Equation redundancy means the adjoint equation map has a nontrivial null vector compatible with the right-hand side.
Lift-kernel degeneracy means distinct lifted points can represent the same conic slack and original point.
Facial degeneracy is equivalent to failure of ambient strict feasibility when the minimal slack face is proper.
special_cases_latex: Duplicating an equality creates equation redundancy without changing \(F\).
Adding a free variable absent from every constraint creates lift-kernel degeneracy.
Embedding a smaller semidefinite cone as a fixed face of a larger one creates facial degeneracy.
immediate_consequences_latex: Equation redundancy can induce nonunique equality multipliers.
Kernel degeneracy prevents unique recovery of lifted variables.
Facial degeneracy can invalidate ambient Slater conditions.
boundary_notes: The three predicates need not occur together.
Primal nonuniqueness caused by the objective is not classified unless it arises from the displayed representation defects.
No inspected source supports this exact three-part taxonomy.
review_flags: The taxonomy is mathematically precise but requires an authoritative source matching its three selected classes.
knowledge_statements.title: Three Degeneracies Induced by Redundancy and Lifting

children.title: Redundant-Formulation Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Degeneracy introduced through redundant constraints or representations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Adjoint-Kernel Criterion for Redundant Equality Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equality constraint re-encoded by an injective residual map, without auxiliary lifting variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g(x)=Ax-b\in Y\) and let \(R:Y\to W\) be injective. Then \(Rg(x)=0\) and \(g(x)=0\) have the same feasible set. A multiplier \(v\in W^*\) for the re-encoded equality enters the Lagrangian through \(R^*v\); consequently multiplier representations are unique modulo \(\ker R^*\), and are nonunique exactly when \(\ker R^*\ne\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An injective redundant encoding preserves an equality-constrained primal problem, while the adjoint kernel is exactly its invisible multiplier space.
assumptions_latex: \(A:X\to Y\) and \(R:Y\to W\) are linear, with \(R\) injective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Primal feasibility is unchanged and multiplier ambiguity is precisely \(\ker R^*\).
knowledge_statements.title: Adjoint-Kernel Criterion for Redundant Equality Representations

assumptions_latex: \(A:X\to Y\) is linear and the equality constraint is \(Ax=b\).
The redundant formulation repeats this equality twice.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal feasible set is unchanged, while the Lagrangian depends on multipliers \((y_1,y_2)\) only through \(y_1+y_2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier degeneracy caused by duplicating an equality constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the duplicated constraints \(Ax=b\) and \(Ax=b\), the Lagrangian is \(L(x,y_1,y_2)=f(x)+\langle y_1+y_2,Ax-b\rangle\). Hence the primal feasible set and objective value equal those of the single-constraint formulation, but every transformation \((y_1,y_2)\mapsto(y_1+w,y_2-w)\) leaves the Lagrangian and dual function unchanged. Whenever one dual-optimal pair exists, the full affine family generated by such \(w\in Y^*\) is dual optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicating an equality leaves the primal problem unchanged but creates an affine family of indistinguishable multipliers.
knowledge_statements.title: Redundant-Formulation Degeneracy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The duplicate-constraint degeneracy is plausible and property is an appropriate role, but it lacks a citation. A sourced version must also introduce f, b, the relevant dual spaces, and the pairing assumptions explicitly.

children.title: Lifted-Formulation Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Degeneracy introduced through auxiliary variables or lifted representations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Free-Auxiliary-Variable Witness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal finite-dimensional witness for optimizer degeneracy introduced by a lift without redundant constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The problem \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R}x^2\) has the unique optimizer \(x=0\). Its exact lift \(\min_{(x,z)\in\mathbb R^2}x^2\), projected by \((x,z)\mapsto x\), has optimizer set \(\{0\}\times\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding an unconstrained auxiliary variable leaves the projected problem unchanged but turns a unique optimizer into an affine family of lifted optimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,z)}x^2=\{0\}\times\mathbb R\) while \(\operatorname*{argmin}_x x^2=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Free-Auxiliary-Variable Witness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimal-Fiber Degeneracy of Exact Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degeneracy caused solely by non-singleton auxiliary fibers of an exact lifted formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P:\widetilde F\to F\) be a surjective linear projection and let \(\widetilde f(w)=f(Pw)\) on \(\widetilde F\). Then \(\inf_{w\in\widetilde F}\widetilde f(w)=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\) and \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{w\in\widetilde F}\widetilde f=P^{-1}(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f)\cap\widetilde F\). Thus an exact lift preserves projected optimizers but preserves uniqueness in the lifted space exactly when every optimal fiber is a singleton.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact lift preserves the primal value and projected optimizers, but a non-singleton auxiliary fiber creates additional lifted optimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(\widetilde F\) are nonempty finite-dimensional convex feasible sets.
\(P(\widetilde F)=F\) and \(\widetilde f=f\circ P\) on \(\widetilde F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Lifted optimizer uniqueness holds exactly when each fiber over an original optimizer is a singleton.

notation.meaning: projection from lifted variables to original variables

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Fiber Degeneracy of Exact Lifts

assumptions_latex: \(B:X\to Z\) is linear and a lift introduces \(z=Bx\).
A second constraint \(C(z-Bx)=0\) is added for a linear map \(C:Z\to W\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\ker C^*\ne\{0\}\), the lifted constraint multipliers are nonunique although the projected feasible set is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual degeneracy from linearly dependent equations in an exact lifted formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The constraints \(z-Bx=0\) and \(C(z-Bx)=0\) project exactly onto the original variables because the first already enforces the second. With multipliers \(u\in Z^*\) and \(v\in W^*\), their Lagrangian contribution is \(\langle u+C^*v,z-Bx\rangle\). Thus it depends only on \(u+C^*v\). In particular, every \(w\in\ker C^*\) generates the indistinguishable multiplier pair \((u,v+w)\), so nontrivial \(\ker C^*\) yields multiplier nonuniqueness without altering primal feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dependent equations in an exact lift preserve projected feasibility but can make the lift multipliers nonunique.
knowledge_statements.title: Lifted-Formulation Degeneracy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The multiplier-nullspace calculation fits the lifted-degeneracy container, but no source is cited. A sourced formulation must specify the vector-space and duality structures needed for C^* and the pairings.

children.title: Redundancy–Lifting Interaction
children.top_down_role: Combined degeneracy effects when redundancy occurs within lifted formulations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Duplicated Lift Residual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical finite-dimensional witness isolating redundancy within a lifting equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Tz=(z,z)\) on \(\mathbb R\), the constraint \(T(z-x)=0\) is equivalent to \(z=x\). Its multipliers \((u_1,u_2)\) enter the Lagrangian only through \(u_1+u_2\), so \((u_1+t,u_2-t)\) is indistinguishable for every \(t\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicating the residual coordinates of an exact lifting equation preserves the lift while creating an affine multiplier family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ker T^*=\{(t,-t):t\in\mathbb R\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Duplicated Lift Residual

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Adjoint-Kernel Criterion for Redundant Lift Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional exact lifting equation encoded with redundant residual coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r(x,z)=z-Bx\in Z\) and let \(T:Z\to W\) be injective. The equation \(Tr(x,z)=0\) is equivalent to the exact lifting equation \(z=Bx\). With multiplier \(v\in W^*\), the Lagrangian depends on \(v\) only through \(T^*v\). Hence its multiplier representation is nonunique exactly when \(\ker T^*\ne\{0\}\); every \(w\in\ker T^*\) leaves the Lagrangian and dual function unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An injective but redundantly codimensioned encoding of a lifting equation is primal-exact, while the kernel of its adjoint is exactly the null multiplier space.
assumptions_latex: \(B:X\to Z\) and \(T:Z\to W\) are linear, with \(T\) injective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal lift is exact, and multiplier degeneracy occurs exactly when \(\ker T^*\ne\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Adjoint-Kernel Criterion for Redundant Lift Encodings

assumptions_latex: An exact lift uses the duplicated equations \(z-Bx=0\) and \(z-Bx=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dual function depends only on \(u_1+u_2\), so lifting and redundancy jointly introduce a null multiplier direction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combined degeneracy when an exact lifting equation is also redundant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The duplicated lifting equations have the same projection \(z=Bx\) as one lifting equation. Their total Lagrangian term is \(\langle u_1+u_2,z-Bx\rangle\). Therefore \((u_1,u_2)\) and \((u_1+w,u_2-w)\) define the same Lagrangian and dual value for every \(w\in Z^*\). Redundancy consequently creates a null direction in the multiplier space introduced by lifting, even when the original formulation has no corresponding multiplier ambiguity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicating a lifting equation combines two harmless primal operations into a nonunique lifted multiplier representation.
knowledge_statements.title: Redundancy–Lifting Interaction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated null multiplier direction correctly describes the redundancy–lifting interaction, but it has no supporting citation and does not fully introduce the spaces and map B.

children.title: Reformulation-Invariance Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Properties that may fail to persist across redundant or lifted reformulations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Invertible Constraint Reparameterization Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp preservation boundary for equality-constraint multiplier representations under linear reparameterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an equality residual \(g(x)\in Y\), replacing \(g(x)=0\) by \(Sg(x)=0\) with a linear bijection \(S:Y\to W\) preserves feasibility and induces the bijective multiplier correspondence \(y=S^*\widetilde y\). Under this correspondence the Lagrangians, dual functions, dual attainment, and multiplier uniqueness agree. If \(S\) is injective but not surjective, primal equivalence remains, while every element of \(\ker S^*\) is an invisible multiplier direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bijective constraint reparameterizations preserve dual certificates; injective non-surjective encodings remain primal-equivalent but can create multiplier degeneracy.
assumptions_latex: The two formulations differ only by the stated linear reparameterization of the same equality residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Bijectivity of \(S\) yields a bijection of multipliers; for injective \(S\), failure of surjectivity is equivalent to \(\ker S^*\ne\{0\}\).
review_flags: claim is limited to equality reparameterizations and does not assert invariance for arbitrary lifts
knowledge_statements.title: Invertible Constraint Reparameterization Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal Invariants of Exact Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional reformulations whose lifted objective factors through the projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(P(\widetilde F)=F\) and \(\widetilde f=f\circ P\) on \(\widetilde F\), then the original and lifted problems have the same infimum. Their minimizers satisfy \(P(\operatorname*{argmin}_{\widetilde F}\widetilde f)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{F}f\) whenever either side is nonempty. These identities alone impose no correspondence between formulation-specific constraint qualifications or multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact projection preserves the primal value and projected minimizers, but it does not by itself preserve qualifications or dual certificates.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(\widetilde F\) are nonempty finite-dimensional feasible sets.
\(P:\widetilde F\to F\) is surjective and \(\widetilde f=f\circ P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Primal values and projected minimizers are invariant; formulation-specific dual properties require additional structure.

notation.meaning: projection from the reformulated feasible set

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Invariants of Exact Projection

assumptions_latex:
\(F\subset X\) and \(\widetilde F\subset X\times Z\) satisfy \(F=\{x:\exists z,
(x,z)\in\widetilde F\}\).
The lifted objective obeys \(\widetilde f(x,z)=f(x)\) on \(\widetilde F\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantities preserved by exact projection versus formulation-dependent dual properties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the stated projection and objective identities, \(\inf_{x\in F}f(x)=\inf_{(x,z)\in\widetilde F}\widetilde f(x,z)\), and primal minimizers correspond after projection, subject to attainment. These identities alone do not preserve interior-based qualifications, uniqueness or existence of multipliers, or attainment of a formulation-specific Lagrange dual. Such dual properties are invariant only under additional regularity and nonredundancy conditions on the reformulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Nonconvex Lagrangian Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An elementary equality-constrained nonconvex problem with a positive finite Lagrangian duality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{-1,0,1\}\), set \(f(-1)=f(1)=0\) and \(f(0)=1\), and impose \(x=0\). The primal value is \(p^*=1\). For an unrestricted equality multiplier \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\), the dual function is \[q(\lambda)=\min_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\lambda x\}=\min\{-\lambda,1,\lambda\}=-|\lambda|.\] Consequently, \[d^*=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R}q(\lambda)=0<p^*=1.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A three-point nonconvex equality-constrained problem has primal value one and Lagrangian dual value zero.
assumptions_latex: Equality multipliers are unrestricted real numbers.
The primal domain, objective, and equality constraint are exactly as stated.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Nonconvex Lagrangian Gap

assumptions_latex: The perturbation value is \(v(u)=\inf\{f(x):g(x)\le u\}\), and conjugates use the standard Euclidean pairing.
\(v\) is proper and the Lagrange dual value is well-defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Lagrange dual value is \(d^*=v^{**}(0)\le v(0)=p^*\); a strict gap occurs exactly when \(v^{**}(0)<v(0)\).
review_flags: biconjugate identity requires source verification of closure conventions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation-value characterization of a nonconvex Lagrangian duality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}\bigl(f(x)+\langle\lambda,g(x)\rangle\bigr)\) with \(\lambda\ge0\), define \(d^*=\sup_{\lambda\ge0}q(\lambda)\). The perturbation representation gives \(d^*=v^{**}(0)\), with the biconjugate interpreted in the chosen finite-dimensional perturbation topology. Therefore \(d^*\le p^*=v(0)\). Nonconvexity can make \(v\) nonconvex or nonclosed at zero, and the Lagrangian gap is \(p^*-d^*=v(0)-v^{**}(0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Lagrange dual sees the closed convex envelope of the perturbation value; a gap occurs when that envelope is lower at zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Lagrangian Duality Gaps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The perturbation-value characterization is appropriate for this duality container, but the identity d^*=v^{**}(0) depends on sign, conjugacy, topology, and extended-value conventions that are not supported by a citation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lagrangian Duality Gap for a Nonconvex Program
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(X\) be a nonempty set and consider \(p^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ g_i(x)\le0\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\ h(x)=0\}\), where no convexity is assumed. For \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\) and \(
u\in\mathbb R^q\), define \(L(x,\lambda,
u)=f(x)+\sum_i\lambda_i g_i(x)+\langle
u,h(x)angle\) and \(q(\lambda,
u)=\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda,
u)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition uses the ordinary Lagrangian dual of a deterministic minimization problem and allows extended-real optimal values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Lagrangian dual value is \[d^*=\sup_{\lambda\ge0,\nu}q(\lambda,\nu),\] and the nonconvex Lagrangian duality gap is \[\Delta_L=p^*-d^*\in[0,+\infty].\] The problem has a positive Lagrangian duality gap when \(p^*,d^*\in\mathbb R\) and \(\Delta_L>0\), and an infinite gap when \(p^*\in\mathbb R\) and \(d^*=-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonconvex Lagrangian duality gap is the primal infimum minus the best lower bound supplied by the Lagrangian dual. A strictly positive finite difference is a positive gap; a finite primal value with dual value negative infinity is an infinite gap.
assumptions_latex: The primal problem is a minimization problem with inequality and equality constraints.
No convexity or constraint qualification is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta_L=p^*-\sup_{\lambda\ge0,\nu}\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda,\nu)\ge0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Zero Lagrangian gap means \(p^*=d^*\), independently of whether the dual supremum is attained.
A positive gap means every Lagrangian lower bound is separated from the primal value by at least \(\Delta_L\).
special_cases_latex: For an unconstrained problem, the construction is trivial and \(d^*=p^*\).
For convex programs satisfying an appropriate qualification, the gap commonly vanishes; that regime is outside the nonconvex pathology emphasized here.
immediate_consequences_latex: A positive gap prevents any ordinary multiplier pair from certifying the exact primal value.
Dual attainment and zero gap are distinct: either may fail without the other.
boundary_notes: Nonconvexity permits but does not imply a positive gap.
This definition does not cover gaps of stronger convex, semidefinite, or moment relaxations unless they coincide with the displayed Lagrangian dual.
No exact inspected source locator was available.
review_flags: Standard definition, but the supplied source hints did not yield an inspected exact locator for this formulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relaxation Exactness Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal and primal-dual tests proving that a convex outer relaxation loses no optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq R\) be the feasible sets of an original minimization problem and an outer convex relaxation, using the same objective \(f\) on \(F\). If a relaxed optimizer \(x_{\mathrm{rel}}\in R\) exists and belongs to \(F\), then \[p^*=p_{\mathrm{rel}}^*=f(x_{\mathrm{rel}}).\] More generally, if \(x\in F\) and a dual-feasible object for the relaxation supplies the lower bound \(d=f(x)\), then \[d=p_{\mathrm{rel}}^*=p^*=f(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxed optimizer feasible for the original problem proves exactness; matching an original feasible value with a relaxed dual bound certifies all three values.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq R\), and both minimization problems use the same objective on \(F\).
The stated relaxed optimizer or dual lower bound exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated conditions imply \(p^*=p_{\mathrm{rel}}^*\), and the matching-bound condition also implies \(d=p_{\mathrm{rel}}^*=p^*\).

notation.meaning: Value of a dual-feasible lower bound for the relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Exactness Certificates

assumptions_latex: A minimization problem has value \(p^*\), and a convex relaxation obtained by enlarging its feasible representation has value \(p_{\mathrm{rel}}^*\).
A dual construction for the relaxation has value \(d^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^*\le p_{\mathrm{rel}}^*\le p^*\) and \(p^*-d^*=(p^*-p_{\mathrm{rel}}^*)+(p_{\mathrm{rel}}^*-d^*)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decomposition of an overall lower-bound gap into relaxation and duality components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because the convex relaxation enlarges the feasible representation for a minimization problem, \(p_{\mathrm{rel}}^*\le p^*\). Weak duality for the relaxed problem gives \(d^*\le p_{\mathrm{rel}}^*\). Hence the total primal-dual gap decomposes as \[p^*-d^*=\bigl(p^*-p_{\mathrm{rel}}^*\bigr)+\bigl(p_{\mathrm{rel}}^*-d^*\bigr).\] The first term is the relaxation gap; the second is the duality gap of the convex relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The total lower-bound gap splits into the loss from convex relaxation and the remaining duality gap of that relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Relaxation Gap Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algebraic gap decomposition is correct once the two weak-duality inequalities hold and property fits the interface container. No citation is supplied, and the phrase 'enlarging its feasible representation' must be formalized sufficiently to guarantee p_rel^*<=p^*.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Value and Recovery Interface for a Convex Relaxation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a possibly nonconvex feasible set, let \(R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and convex with \(F\subseteq R\), and let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be the common objective. Set \(p_F=\inf_F f\) and \(p_R=\inf_R f\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The interface records the relaxation bound, its additive gap, and whether a relaxed solution recovers an original feasible optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The convex-relaxation gap interface is the tuple \[\mathcal I(F,R,f)=\bigl(p_R,\Delta_R,\mathcal X_{\mathrm{rec}}\bigr),\qquad \Delta_R=p_F-p_R,\] where \[\mathcal X_{\mathrm{rec}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in R}f(x)\cap F.\] The relaxation is value-exact if \(\Delta_R=0\), strongly recoverable if \(\mathcal X_{\mathrm{rec}}\ne\varnothing\), and inexact if \(\Delta_R>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex-relaxation interface consists of the relaxed bound, the difference between the original and relaxed values, and the original-feasible members of the relaxed optimizer set. It distinguishes equality of values from actual recovery of an original optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq R\) and \(R\) is closed and convex.
The original and relaxed problems use the same objective.
The minimization convention is used, so \(p_R\le p_F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta_R\ge0\); value exactness is \(\Delta_R=0\), while recoverability is \(\operatorname*{argmin}_R f\cap F\ne\varnothing\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Strong recoverability means that some relaxed optimizer is feasible and optimal for the original problem.
When both values are positive, a multiplicative interface may additionally report \(p_F/p_R\), but the additive gap remains defined without positivity.
special_cases_latex: For linear \(f\) and \(R=\overline{\operatorname{conv}}F\), value exactness holds whenever the relevant infima agree under convexification, while attainment may still differ.
For an integral model relaxed to a convex set, \(\mathcal X_{\mathrm{rec}}\) contains precisely the relaxed optimizers satisfying the original integrality restrictions.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every relaxed feasible point supplies a lower-bound problem, but only points in \(\mathcal X_{\mathrm{rec}}\) solve the original problem.
Zero gap without a recovered optimizer is weaker than strong recoverability.
boundary_notes: The definition does not prescribe a rounding rule for nonrecoverable relaxed solutions.
No inspected supplied source states this exact interface tuple.
review_flags: Requires a source matching the combined bound-gap-recovery interface.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual–Gap–Certificate Duality Interface
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For the canonical linear pair \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax\ge b,\ x\ge0\}\) and \(\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty\le c,\ y\ge0\}\), define primal residual \(r_p=(b-Ax)_+\), dual residual \(r_d=(A^Ty-c)_+\), and gap \(g=c^Tx-b^Ty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This node is treated as a navigation-level mathematical interface. It defines quantities exposed to computational methods but contains no update rule, convergence rate, or complexity claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A computational duality interface is the map \[\mathfrak I(x,y)=\bigl(r_p,r_d,g,\sigma_p,\sigma_d\bigr),\] where \(r_p\) and \(r_d\) measure primal and dual feasibility, \(g\) is the primal–dual objective gap, and \(\sigma_p,\sigma_d\) are optional normalized infeasibility-certificate margins. For feasible \((x,y)\), weak duality gives \(g\ge0\); the exact optimality interface is \[r_p=0,\quad r_d=0,\quad g=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A computational duality interface exposes primal feasibility residuals, dual feasibility residuals, the objective gap, and optional certificate margins. It identifies exact primal–dual optimality by simultaneous vanishing of both residuals and the gap, without specifying how an algorithm produces such a pair.
assumptions_latex: The certificate margins, when used, are normalized to remove positive scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface reports exact primal–dual optimality when \(r_p=r_d=0\) and \(g=0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For feasible \(x,y\), \(g=0\) is equality in weak duality.
Complementarity may replace the scalar gap because \(g=x^T(c-A^Ty)+y^T(Ax-b)\) for feasible pairs.
special_cases_latex: For conic programs, positive parts are replaced by distances to the primal and dual cones.
For equality-form linear programs, \(r_p=Ax-b\) and dual feasibility includes the appropriate slack.
immediate_consequences_latex: The tuple separates feasibility failure from objective-gap failure.
A termination or recovery mechanism may consume this interface, but such mechanisms are not part of the definition.
boundary_notes: Numerical tolerances and scaling policies are implementation choices and are excluded.
The interface does not claim convergence of any computational method.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact and Approximate Lagrangian Residual Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-oracle interface for equality-constrained convex optimization; update rules, stopping rules, and convergence guarantees are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X,Y\) be finite-dimensional real spaces, let \(A:X\to Y\) be linear, let \(b\in Y\), and let \(f:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be proper. For \(y\in Y^*\), define \(L(x,y)=f(x)+\langle y,Ax-b\rangle\) and \(q(y)=\inf_xL(x,y)\). If \(q(y)>-\infty\) and \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) satisfies \(L(\bar x,y)\le q(y)+\varepsilon\) for \(\varepsilon\ge0\), then
\[
q(z)\le q(y)+\langle z-y,A\bar x-b\rangle+\varepsilon\qquad\forall z\in Y^*.
\]
Thus \(A\bar x-b\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-supergradient oracle output for \(q\) at \(y\). When \(\varepsilon=0\), an attained Lagrangian minimum supplies an exact supergradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An epsilon-accurate Lagrangian minimizer returns the constraint residual as an epsilon-supergradient of the dual function; exact minimization is the zero-error case.
assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are finite-dimensional real spaces and \(A:X\to Y\) is linear.
\(L(\bar x,y)\le q(y)+\varepsilon\) for some \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q(z)\le q(y)+\langle z-y,A\bar x-b\rangle+\varepsilon\quad\forall z\in Y^*.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact and Approximate Lagrangian Residual Oracles

assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is proper and the primal problem is \(\inf\{f(x):Ax=b\}\).
For each iterate \(y_k\), an exact minimizer \(x_k\in\arg\min_x\{f(x)+\langle y_k,Ax-b\rangle\}\) exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update \(y_{k+1}=y_k+\alpha_k(Ax_k-b)\) is supergradient ascent on the concave dual function.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic dual supergradient method for linear equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize any \(y_0\in Y^*\). At iteration \(k\), compute \(x_k\in\arg\min_x\bigl(f(x)+\langle y_k,Ax-b\rangle\bigr)\), set \(s_k=Ax_k-b\), and update \(y_{k+1}=y_k+\alpha_k s_k\). Then \(s_k\) is a supergradient of \(q(y)=\inf_x\bigl(f(x)+\langle y,Ax-b\rangle\bigr)\) at \(y_k\). Stop under a prescribed residual, dual-progress, or iteration rule and return the selected dual iterate and associated primal candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing the Lagrangian supplies a dual supergradient equal to the constraint residual, which drives dual ascent.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X,Y\) be finite-dimensional real spaces, \(A:X\to Y\) linear, \(b\in Y\), and \(f:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) proper. Define \(L(x,y)=f(x)+\langle y,Ax-b\rangle\) and \(q(y)=\inf_x L(x,y)\). \(\rho>0\), and each augmented-Lagrangian subproblem attains its minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Alternating augmented-Lagrangian minimization and \(y_{k+1}=y_k+\rho(Ax_{k+1}-b)\) defines the method-of-multipliers interface.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained quadratic augmented Lagrangian and multiplier update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(L_\rho(x,y)=f(x)+\langle y,Ax-b\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Ax-b\rVert^2\). Starting from \(y_0\), compute \[x_{k+1}\in\arg\min_x L_\rho(x,y_k),\qquad y_{k+1}=y_k+\rho(Ax_{k+1}-b).\] Stop according to prescribed primal-residual and dual-progress tolerances, and output \((x_{k+1},y_{k+1})\). The quadratic term regularizes constraint violation while the multiplier update retains the dual interpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method of multipliers minimizes a quadratic augmented Lagrangian and then updates the multiplier using the equality residual.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratically Augmented Lagrangian Dual Function
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), and let \(g:X\to\mathbb R^m\). For perturbation \(u\in\mathbb R^m\), write \(C_u=\{x\in X:g(x)\le u\}\), and fix \(c>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is the inequality-constrained quadratic augmented-duality construction. It defines the interface but no multiplier-update method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[p_c(u)=\inf_{x\in C_u}\left(f(x)+\frac c2\|u\|^2\right),\qquad q_c(\mu)=\inf_{u\in\mathbb R^m}\bigl(p_c(u)+\mu^Tu\bigr).\] For \(j=1,\ldots,m\), set \[g_j^+(x,\mu,c)=\max\{-\mu_j/c,\ g_j(x)\}.\] Then the augmented-duality interface is \[L_c(x,\mu)=f(x)+\mu^Tg^+(x,\mu,c)+\frac c2\|g^+(x,\mu,c)\|^2,\qquad q_c(\mu)=\inf_{x\in X}L_c(x,\mu).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The augmented-duality interface adds a quadratic penalty to right-hand-side perturbations, then dualizes the perturbed value function. Componentwise minimization over the perturbation yields an augmented Lagrangian whose infimum over the primal variable is the augmented dual function.
assumptions_latex: Infima are interpreted in the extended-real sense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_c(\mu)=\inf_{x\in X}L_c(x,\mu)\) with \(L_c\) and \(g^+\) as displayed.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The augmented perturbation satisfies \(p_c(0)=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ g(x)\le0\}\).
The inner perturbation minimizer has components \(u_j=g_j^+(x,\mu,c)\).
special_cases_latex: For equality constraints \(Ax=b\), the familiar form is \(f(x)+\langle y,Ax-b\rangle+(c/2)\|Ax-b\|^2\).
If \(X\) is compact and the data are continuous, the augmented dual function is often finite-valued.
immediate_consequences_latex: Quadratic augmentation leaves the unperturbed primal value unchanged.
The augmented dual may be better regularized than the ordinary Lagrangian dual, but no smoothness claim is included here.
boundary_notes: The penalty parameter must be positive.
Algorithmic updates and convergence properties are outside this node.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal–Dual Inclusion System for the Dual Proximal Step
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expresses the dual proximal inclusion as a multiplier residual equation coupled with convex Fermat inclusions for the two primal blocks. It is an augmented-duality optimality representation rather than a general Fermat theorem or an ADMM iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \rho>0, and let h_1 and h_2 be proper, closed, convex functions. Then
\[
0\in-A\partial h_1^*(-A^T y^{k+1})-B\partial h_2^*(-B^T y^{k+1})+c+\frac1\rho(y^{k+1}-y^k)
\]
holds if and only if there exist x^{k+1}\in\mathbb R^n and z^{k+1}\in\mathbb R^p satisfying
\[
y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c),
\]
\[
0\in A^T\bigl(y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c)\bigr)+\partial h_1(x^{k+1}),
\]
and
\[
0\in B^T\bigl(y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c)\bigr)+\partial h_2(z^{k+1}).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conjugate dual-proximal inclusion is equivalent to a residual multiplier update and one convex subgradient Fermat inclusion for each primal block, with both block conditions evaluated at the updated multiplier.
assumptions_latex: h_1:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ and }h_2:\mathbb R^p\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ are proper, closed, and convex}
A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\quad B\in\mathbb R^{m\times p},\quad c\in\mathbb R^m
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The dual proximal inclusion holds}\iff\exists(x^{k+1},z^{k+1})\text{ satisfying the multiplier equation and the two displayed primal subgradient inclusions}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the objective \(h_1(x)+h_2(z)\) and equality residual \(Ax+Bz-c\), the augmented Lagrangian is
\[
L_{\rho}(x,z;y)=h_1(x)+h_2(z)+\langle y,Ax+Bz-c\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax+Bz-c\|^2.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The augmented Lagrangian is the composite objective plus the multiplier pairing with the equality residual and one half rho times the squared norm of that residual.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal-Block Representation of the Dual Proximal Inclusion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Converts the conjugate-subgradient inclusion for a multiplier-dual proximal step into a residual multiplier update and two primal block minimization conditions. This is an augmented-duality correspondence, not an alternating ADMM update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \rho>0, and let h_1 and h_2 be proper, closed, convex functions. Then
\[
0\in-A\partial h_1^*(-A^T y^{k+1})-B\partial h_2^*(-B^T y^{k+1})+c+\frac1\rho(y^{k+1}-y^k)
\]
holds if and only if there exist x^{k+1}\in\mathbb R^n and z^{k+1}\in\mathbb R^p such that
\[
y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c),
\]
\[
x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\{\langle A^T y^{k+1},x\rangle+h_1(x)\},
\]
and
\[
z^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{z\in\mathbb R^p}\{\langle B^T y^{k+1},z\rangle+h_2(z)\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual proximal inclusion is equivalent to the existence of primal block minimizers evaluated at the new multiplier together with the residual multiplier update yᵏ⁺¹=yᵏ+ρ(Axᵏ⁺¹+Bzᵏ⁺¹−c). This does not yet define alternating ADMM.
assumptions_latex: h_1:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ and }h_2:\mathbb R^p\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ are proper, closed, and convex}
A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\quad B\in\mathbb R^{m\times p},\quad c\in\mathbb R^m
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\in-A\partial h_1^*(-A^T y^{k+1})-B\partial h_2^*(-B^T y^{k+1})+c+\frac1\rho(y^{k+1}-y^k)\iff\exists(x^{k+1},z^{k+1})\text{ satisfying the multiplier update and both block argmin conditions}

assumptions_latex: The primal problem is \(\inf\{\sum_{i=1}^N f_i(x_i):\sum_{i=1}^N A_i x_i=b\}\).
Each \(f_i\) is proper and each block infimum defining the dual function is meaningful.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dualizing the coupling equality yields \(q(y)=-\langle y,b\rangle+\sum_{i=1}^N\inf_{x_i}\bigl(f_i(x_i)+\langle A_i^*y,x_i\rangle\bigr)\), which separates by block.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable dual representation obtained by dualizing a single coupling equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With multiplier \(y\) for \(\sum_i A_i x_i=b\), the Lagrangian is \(L(x_1,\ldots,x_N,y)=\sum_{i=1}^N\bigl(f_i(x_i)+\langle A_i^*y,x_i\rangle\bigr)-\langle y,b\rangle\). Therefore its infimum separates as \[q(y)=-\langle y,b\rangle+\sum_{i=1}^N\inf_{x_i}\bigl(f_i(x_i)+\langle A_i^*y,x_i\rangle\bigr).\] Maximizing \(q\) coordinates the otherwise independent block subproblems through the shared multiplier \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing a coupling equality turns a separable primal objective into independent block subproblems coordinated by one multiplier.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(i=1,\ldots,N\), let \(X_i\) and \(Y\) be real Hilbert spaces, let \(f_i:X_i\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), and let \(A_i:X_i\to Y\) be bounded linear. Consider \(\inf\{\sum_i f_i(x_i):\sum_iA_ix_i=b\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition records the exact mathematical decomposition produced by dualizing a shared linear coupling constraint. No coordination algorithm is included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(y\in Y\), define \[L(x_1,\ldots,x_N;y)=\sum_{i=1}^N f_i(x_i)+\left\langle y,\sum_{i=1}^NA_ix_i-b\right\rangle.\] The decomposition-by-dualization interface is \[q(y)=-\langle y,b\rangle+\sum_{i=1}^N q_i(y),\qquad q_i(y)=\inf_{x_i\in X_i}\bigl(f_i(x_i)+\langle A_i^*y,x_i\rangle\bigr),\] equivalently \[q(y)=-\langle y,b\rangle-\sum_{i=1}^N f_i^*(-A_i^*y).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing the common linear coupling constraint separates the Lagrangian infimum into independent block infima. The interface exposes one shared multiplier, one local dual contribution per block, and the sum that forms the global dual objective.
assumptions_latex: The objective is additively separable across the blocks.
Each \(A_i\) is bounded linear, with adjoint \(A_i^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x_1,\ldots,x_N}L(x_1,\ldots,x_N;y)=-\langle y,b\rangle-\sum_i f_i^*(-A_i^*y)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The primal response set factors as \(\prod_i\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_i}(f_i(x_i)+\langle A_i^*y,x_i\rangle)\) whenever every local argmin is nonempty.
The global dual problem is \(\sup_{y\in Y}q(y)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(A_i\) selects a resource contribution, \(y\) is the common resource price.
With two blocks and \(A_1=I,A_2=-I\), the constraint is consensus \(x_1=x_2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Evaluation of \(q(y)\) reduces to independent local infima plus one affine term.
Exact primal recovery still requires satisfaction of the coupling constraint and any applicable duality conditions.
boundary_notes: Additional coupling in the objective destroys this exact additive decomposition unless it is separately represented.
No inspected supplied source locator matched this exact Hilbert-space interface.

assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone with dual cone \(K^*\).

The primal-dual conic pair is \(\min\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=b,
x\in K\}\) and \(\max\{\langle b,y\rangle:A^*y+s=c,
s\in K^*\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The homogeneous equations combine primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and the duality gap in one conic feasibility system.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard homogeneous self-dual equations for a primal-dual conic pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A homogeneous self-dual embedding seeks \((x,y,s,\tau,\kappa)\) satisfying \[Ax=b\tau,\qquad A^*y+s=c\tau,\qquad \langle c,x\rangle-\langle b,y\rangle+\kappa=0,\] together with \(x\in K\), \(s\in K^*\), and \(\tau,\kappa\ge0\). The equations imply \(\langle x,s\rangle+\tau\kappa=0\). When \(\tau>0\), scaling by \(\tau\) recovers primal-dual feasibility; when \(\tau=0\), nonzero limiting components may instead encode infeasibility information under additional classification conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A homogeneous conic system packages primal feasibility, dual feasibility, optimality, and potential infeasibility information into one embedding.
knowledge_statements.title: Homogeneous Self-Dual Embedding Interface

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Skew-Symmetric Homogeneous Embedding of a Linear Primal–Dual Pair
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \((P)\ \min\{c^Tx:Ax\ge b,\ x\ge0\}\) and \((D)\ \max\{b^Ty:A^Ty\le c,\ y\ge0\}\), with \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\). Introduce \(\tau\ge0\), \(z=(y,x,\tau)\), and \[M=\begin{bmatrix}0&A&-b\\-A^T&0&c\\b^T&-c^T&0\end{bmatrix}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition is the finite-dimensional linear-optimization embedding interface. It states the homogeneous skew system and its positive-scale recovery map, not an interior-point algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The homogeneous self-dual embedding interface is the feasibility system \[Mz\ge0,\qquad z\ge0,\qquad z=(y,x,\tau),\] where \(M^T=-M\). A solution with \(\tau>0\) recovers the scaled pair \[\bar x=x/\tau,\qquad \bar y=y/\tau,\] satisfying \[A\bar x\ge b,\quad \bar x\ge0,\quad A^T\bar y\le c,\quad \bar y\ge0,\quad c^T\bar x=b^T\bar y.\] The system is homogeneous because every positive multiple of a solution is again a solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The embedding combines primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and zero duality gap into one homogeneous inequality system with a skew-symmetric matrix. Any embedded solution whose homogenizing coordinate is positive rescales to a primal–dual feasible pair with equal objective values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Mz\ge0\), \(z\ge0\), and \(\tau>0\) recover \((x/\tau,y/\tau)\) as an optimal primal–dual pair with zero gap.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The three block inequalities are \(Ax-b\tau\ge0\), \(-A^Ty+c\tau\ge0\), and \(b^Ty-c^Tx\ge0\).
Skew symmetry gives \(z^TMz=0\), so nonnegative complementary block products encode the zero-gap relation.
special_cases_latex: Setting \(\tau=1\) yields the ordinary simultaneous primal-feasibility, dual-feasibility, and zero-gap system.
An adapted embedding may add a variable and right-hand side to obtain a known strictly feasible starting point.
immediate_consequences_latex: Positive rescaling does not change the recovered primal–dual pair.
Solutions with \(\tau=0\) do not directly recover finite primal and dual points and require separate status interpretation.
boundary_notes: The zero vector is always a formal homogeneous solution and is not a recovery point.
This record does not state a complete classification of all zero-scale rays or an algorithm for finding a nonzero solution.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Absolute-gap primal-dual termination and recovery interface
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and consider \(p^\star=\inf\{f_0(x):x\in\mathcal D,\ f_i(x)\leq0\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\ h_j(x)=0\ (j=1,\ldots,q)\}\). Its Lagrangian and dual function are \(L(x,\lambda,
u)=f_0(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i f_i(x)+\sum_{j=1}^q
u_jh_j(x)\) and \(g(\lambda,
u)=\inf_{z\in\mathcal D}L(z,\lambda,
u)\). Define the primal feasible set \(\mathcal F_P\) by the displayed constraints and the finite-valued dual feasible set \(\mathcal F_D=\{(\lambda,
u)\in\mathbb R_+^m	imes\mathbb R^q:g(\lambda,
u)>-\infty\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Lagrangian convex programming with exact primal and dual feasibility and an absolute objective-gap tolerance. The certificate itself relies only on weak duality; convexity and a constraint qualification are relevant to whether arbitrarily small tolerances can be attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\epsilon\geq0\), the primal-dual termination-recovery interface is the partial map \(\mathcal I_\epsilon:\mathcal D	imes\mathbb R^m	imes\mathbb R^qightharpoonup \mathcal F_P	imes\mathcal P(\overline{\mathbb R})	imes\mathbb R_+\) defined on precisely those triples \((x,\lambda,
u)\) satisfying \(x\in\mathcal F_P\), \((\lambda,
u)\in\mathcal F_D\), and \(\Delta(x,\lambda,
u):=f_0(x)-g(\lambda,
u)\leq\epsilon\). On this domain, \[\mathcal I_\epsilon(x,\lambda,
u)= igl(x_{\mathrm{rec}},I_{\mathrm{val}},\Delta igr):=\left(x,\,[g(\lambda,
u),f_0(x)],\,f_0(x)-g(\lambda,
u)ight).\] Thus the termination predicate is \(\operatorname{Stop}_\epsilon(x,\lambda,
u)\iff x\in\mathcal F_P,\ (\lambda,
u)\in\mathcal F_D,\ \Delta(x,\lambda,
u)\leq\epsilon\); its recovered primal point is \(x_{\mathrm{rec}}=x\), and its recovered value enclosure is \(I_{\mathrm{val}}=[g(\lambda,
u),f_0(x)]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonnegative absolute tolerance ε, the interface accepts exactly a primal-feasible point x and a finite-valued dual-feasible pair (λ,ν) whose primal-dual objective gap Δ = f₀(x) − g(λ,ν) is at most ε. Upon acceptance it terminates and returns the same feasible point as the recovered primal point, the interval from the dual value g(λ,ν) to the primal value f₀(x) as a certified enclosure of the optimal value, and Δ as the certificate width. If either feasibility condition or the gap test fails, the interface has no certified return.
assumptions_latex: The interface is evaluated using exact primal feasibility, exact dual feasibility \(\lambda\geq0\) with \(g(\lambda,\nu)>-\infty\), and the exact values \(f_0(x)\) and \(g(\lambda,\nu)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(\operatorname{dom}\mathcal I_\epsilon=\{(x,\lambda,
u):x\in\mathcal F_P,\ (\lambda,
u)\in\mathcal F_D,\ f_0(x)-g(\lambda,
u)\leq\epsilon\}\), and for every accepted triple, \(\mathcal I_\epsilon(x,\lambda,
u)=(x,[g(\lambda,
u),f_0(x)],f_0(x)-g(\lambda,
u))\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a primal-dual feasible triple, \(\operatorname{Stop}_\epsilon(x,\lambda,\nu)\) is equivalent to \(\operatorname{width}(I_{\mathrm{val}})\leq\epsilon\).

For a primal-dual feasible triple, the gap test is equivalent to the simultaneous bounds \(0\leq f_0(x)-p^\star\leq\epsilon\) and \(0\leq d^\star-g(\lambda,\nu)\leq\epsilon\), together with the value enclosure \(g(\lambda,\nu)\leq d^\star\leq p^\star\leq f_0(x)\).
special_cases_latex:
At \(\epsilon=0\), acceptance means \(f_0(x)=g(\lambda,
u)\); consequently \(x\) and \((\lambda,
u)\) are respectively primal and dual optimal and \(p^\star=d^\star=f_0(x)=g(\lambda,
u)\).
If an algorithm generates primal-dual feasible iterates \((x^k,\lambda^k,\nu^k)\), its absolute-gap stopping index is \(K_\epsilon=\inf\{k:f_0(x^k)-g(\lambda^k,\nu^k)\leq\epsilon\}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every accepted recovered point satisfies \(f_0(x_{\mathrm{rec}})-p^\star\leq\Delta\leq\epsilon\), so it is \(\epsilon\)-suboptimal.
The returned interval contains both optimal values and has width \(\Delta\): \(g(\lambda,\nu)\leq d^\star\leq p^\star\leq f_0(x)\) and \(\operatorname{width}(I_{\mathrm{val}})=\Delta\).
boundary_notes: An infeasible iterate is outside this exact interface even when its residuals are small; residual-based approximate-feasibility termination requires a separate error model.
Strong duality is unnecessary for validity of an accepted certificate, but a positive optimal duality gap can prevent acceptance for tolerances below that gap.
The relative-gap tests that divide by a positive dual bound or by a negative primal bound are nearby variants, not part of this absolute-gap definition.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces, \(A:X\to Y\) is linear, and \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), \(g:Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper closed convex functions.
The primal and dual values are finite at the candidate pair \((x,y)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le P(x)-p^\star\le G(x,y)\) and \(0\le d^\star-D(y)\le G(x,y)\); hence \(G(x,y)\le\varepsilon\) certifies both errors at most \(\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the Fenchel pair \(P(x)=f(x)+g(Ax)\) and \(D(y)=-f^*(-A^*y)-g^*(y)\), define
\[
G(x,y)=P(x)-D(y)=f(x)+g(Ax)+f^*(-A^*y)+g^*(y).
\]
Weak duality gives \(G(x,y)\ge 0\). Moreover, whenever \(p^\star=\inf_xP(x)\) and \(d^\star=\sup_yD(y)\) are finite,
\[
P(x)-p^\star\le G(x,y),\qquad d^\star-D(y)\le G(x,y).
\]
Thus the computable test \(G(x,y)\le\varepsilon\) is an absolute primal–dual stopping certificate. Under strong duality, it also bounds the sum of the two objective errors exactly by \(G(x,y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite primal–dual gap certifies that both candidate objective errors are no larger than the gap; stopping at gap ε therefore gives ε-accuracy.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Stopping Criteria

children.top_down_role: Interpretation of dual or embedded outputs as primal solution information.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces, \(A:X\to Y\) is linear, and \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), \(g:Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper closed convex functions.
The supplied point \(y\in Y\) satisfies \(f^*(-A^*y)<+infty\) and \(g^*(y)<+infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Whenever \((x,z)\in\mathcal R_P(y)\), the point \(x\in X\) is a primal candidate; if \(Ax=z\), then \(-A^*y\in\partial f(x)\) and \(y\in\partial g(Ax)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Possibly empty set-valued recovery from a dual point through Fenchel equality and coupling.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(y\in Y\), define the possibly empty primal recovery correspondence
\[
\mathcal R_P(y)=\{(x,z)\in X\times Y:-A^*y\in\partial f(x),\ z\in\partial g^*(y)\}.
\]
The first inclusion is equivalent to
\[
x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in X}\{f(u)+\langle Au,y\rangle\},
\]
and the second means that \(z\) realizes Fenchel equality for \(g\) and \(g^*\). For any \((x,z)\in\mathcal R_P(y)\), the recovered primal candidate is \(x\), with coupling residual \(r_P=Ax-z\). If \(r_P=0\), conjugate-subgradient inversion gives \(y\in\partial g(Ax)\); together with \(-A^*y\in\partial f(x)\), this is the primal–dual optimality system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the recovery correspondence is nonempty, a primal candidate is obtained by minimizing the Lagrangian at the dual point and selecting a conjugate subgradient. Equality between its image and that subgradient completes the optimality conditions.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Recovery Interface

assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces, \(A:X\to Y\) is linear, and \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), \(g:Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper closed convex functions.
The supplied point \(x\in X\) satisfies \(f(x)<+infty\) and \(g(Ax)<+infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Whenever \((y,u)\in\mathcal R_D(x)\), the point \(y\in Y\) is a dual candidate; if \(u+A^*y=0\), then \(-A^*y\in\partial f(x)\) and \(y\in\partial g(Ax)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in X\), define the possibly empty dual recovery correspondence
\[
\mathcal R_D(x)=\{(y,u)\in Y\times X:y\in\partial g(Ax),\ u\in\partial f(x)\}.
\]
The first inclusion is equivalent to
\[
y\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{v\in Y}\{\langle Ax,v\rangle-g^*(v)\}.
\]
For any \((y,u)\in\mathcal R_D(x)\), the recovered dual candidate is \(y\), with stationarity residual \(r_D=u+A^*y\). If \(r_D=0\), then \(-A^*y\in\partial f(x)\); together with \(y\in\partial g(Ax)\), this is the primal–dual optimality system and makes \(y\) an exact dual recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the recovery correspondence is nonempty, a dual candidate is obtained from a subgradient of the outer function at the primal image. A compatible subgradient of the primal term with zero stationarity residual completes the primal–dual optimality conditions.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Recovery Interface

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The gap decomposes into two Fenchel–Young residuals:
\[
G(x,y)=f(x)+f^*(-A^*y)+\langle x,A^*y\rangle+g(Ax)+g^*(y)-\langle Ax,y\rangle.
\]
Both summands are nonnegative. Consequently, \(G(x,y)=0\) if and only if \(-A^*y\in\partial f(x)\) and \(y\in\partial g(Ax)\). Equivalently, exact gap-based stopping holds precisely when \(x\) is recoverable from \(y\), \(y\) is recoverable from \(x\), and their coupling and stationarity residuals can both be chosen zero. Thus the stopping certificate and the two recovery interfaces select the same exact primal–dual solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero primal–dual gap is equivalent to both Fenchel recovery conditions, so exact termination and mutually consistent primal and dual recovery identify the same solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Stopping–Recovery Consistency

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quantitative Gap–Recovery Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate consistency between the Fenchel gap and its two component Fenchel–Young recovery residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P(x)=f(x)+g(Ax)\), \(D(y)=-f^*(-A^*y)-g^*(y)\), and define \[R_f(x,y)=f(x)+f^*(-A^*y)+\langle x,A^*y\rangle,\qquad R_g(x,y)=g(Ax)+g^*(y)-\langle Ax,y\rangle.\] If all terms are finite, then \(G(x,y)=P(x)-D(y)=R_f(x,y)+R_g(x,y)\), where \(R_f,R_g\ge0\). Consequently, \[G(x,y)\le\varepsilon\Longrightarrow R_f(x,y)\le\varepsilon,\quad R_g(x,y)\le\varepsilon,\] equivalently \(-A^*y\in\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\) and \(y\in\partial_\varepsilon g(Ax)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small Fenchel primal-dual gap bounds both Fenchel–Young recovery residuals and yields the corresponding epsilon-subgradient inclusions.
assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces and \(A:X\to Y\) is linear.
\(f\) and \(g\) are proper closed convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G(x,y)\le\varepsilon\Longrightarrow -A^*y\in\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\ \text{and}\ y\in\partial_\varepsilon g(Ax)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Quantitative Gap–Recovery Consistency
